steps.instructions: Confirm the sterilizer is energized and the display, indicators, and controls have completed normal startup. Check for an obvious facility power interruption or upstream electrical issue. Do not open electrical enclosures solely to investigate a cycle-start complaint unless required later under authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: The sterilizer remains powered with a stable user interface and no obvious loss of facility power. If power is unstable, correct the external supply issue before continuing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Door and Door Area
steps.instructions: Verify the door is fully closed and there is no tray, rack, packaging material, debris, or other obstruction preventing complete closure. Observe whether the sterilizer recognizes the expected closed or locked condition. Do not bypass or defeat door interlocks. Expected outcome: The door closes normally and the sterilizer recognizes the required door condition. If removing an external obstruction restores proper recognition and the cycle starts normally, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Verify Cycle Selection and Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm an appropriate cycle can be selected using normal operator controls. Check the displayed status for any indication that the sterilizer is not ready, is waiting for a condition, or requires acknowledgment of an existing message. Do not change validated cycle parameters simply to force the unit to start. Expected outcome: A valid cycle is selected and the sterilizer indicates that it is ready to begin. If an incorrectly selected or incomplete control sequence was the cause and normal cycle initiation is restored, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Check Accessible Utility Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that facility utilities required for normal operation are available at the sterilizer. Depending on installation, this may include steam, water, compressed air, electrical power, or drainage support. Look for obvious closed external isolation valves, facility outages, or utility work affecting the sterilizer. Expected outcome: Required utilities appear available and no external interruption is identified. If an external utility condition is corrected and the cycle starts normally, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Inspect External Connections and Surrounding Conditions
steps.instructions: Check accessible external utility connections and the area around the sterilizer for: Visible leakage. Damaged hoses or piping. Disconnected accessible cables. Water accumulation. Unusual heat, odor, or noise. Recent construction or utility work. Do not disassemble internal valve, control, or steam components during this step. Expected outcome: No obvious external condition is preventing operation. Any unsafe leak, electrical concern, burning odor, or significant physical damage requires removal from service.

steps.title: 8. Power-Cycle Only When Operationally Appropriate
steps.instructions: If permitted by facility procedure and no load is being actively processed, perform a normal shutdown and restart using approved controls. Do not remove power during an active sterilization process solely as a troubleshooting shortcut. Expected outcome: The sterilizer completes startup normally and accepts a cycle-start command. If normal operation returns and remains repeatable, perform final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate unloaded or facility-approved test process, verify that the sterilizer accepts cycle selection, recognizes the door condition, starts normally, and transitions into the expected initial cycle phase. Follow facility and manufacturer requirements before returning the unit to production. Expected outcome: The cycle begins consistently without unexpected messages or abnormal behavior. If successful, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved No-Start Condition
steps.instructions: If power, door condition, cycle selection, accessible utilities, external connections, and normal startup have been verified but the sterilizer still will not begin a cycle, stop external troubleshooting. Potential service-level categories include door-interlock sensing, control input, utility-control, safety-interlock, or internal control-system problems. Expected outcome: An unresolved sterilizer is removed from service rather than repeatedly attempted in clinical production.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the AMSCO 600 Series powered on and allowed cycle selection but would not start.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found packaging material preventing the chamber door from fully closing and achieving the recognized closed condition.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the obstruction, verified proper door closure, started an approved test cycle, and confirmed normal cycle initiation before returning the sterilizer to service.

helpfulDetails: Cycle selected when the failure occurred.
Whether one or all cycles were affected.

title: STERIS AMSCO 600 Series Sterilizer - Door Will Not Close, Lock, or Recognize Closed Position
description: Use this guide for door closure, locking, or closed-position recognition problems caused by obstruction, loading, alignment, controls, or service-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Safety and Prevent Unsafe Operation
steps.instructions: Do not operate or attempt to bypass a sterilizer door interlock that does not function reliably. Do not force the door closed or defeat locking mechanisms. If sterile processing must continue, transfer the workload to another verified sterilizer. Expected outcome: No load is processed using a sterilizer with uncertain door containment or interlock status.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Door Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the door: Physically will not close. Closes but will not lock. Locks mechanically but is not recognized as closed. Opens unexpectedly. Fails only from one side on a pass-through installation. Produces a message or alarm. Observe the condition without forcing the mechanism. Expected outcome: The complaint is narrowed to physical closure, locking, recognition, or control behavior. If normal operation is reproduced repeatedly, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Chamber and Doorway Obstructions
steps.instructions: Inspect the chamber opening, door edge, loading equipment, racks, carts, packaging materials, and surrounding area. Remove any external object preventing full travel of the door. Look for trapped wrappers, tape, labels, biological indicators, debris, or mispositioned loading hardware. Expected outcome: The door path is clear. If removing an obstruction restores normal closure and locking, troubleshooting can stop after repeated verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Load and Loading Equipment Position
steps.instructions: Confirm the load, rack, transfer carriage, or loading cart is fully positioned and not protruding into the door path. Look for bent, displaced, or incorrectly seated external loading components. Expected outcome: Loading equipment and the load remain completely clear of the door. If repositioning restores proper operation, verify several normal door cycles and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Door Sealing Surfaces
steps.instructions: With the sterilizer safe and idle, visually inspect accessible door and chamber sealing surfaces for debris, residue, or obvious physical damage. Do not remove internal door components or adjust locking hardware without authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: Accessible sealing and contact areas are clean and unobstructed. Significant deformation, damaged hardware, or compromised sealing surfaces requires removal from service.

steps.title: 6. Verify Normal Door Controls
steps.instructions: Operate the door only using the normal approved controls. Check whether the controls respond consistently and whether the displayed door status changes appropriately. For double-door configurations, confirm the opposite door is in the required safe condition before expecting the affected door to operate. Expected outcome: Door controls respond and the displayed status corresponds to actual door position. If correct operation returns after resolving a valid opposing-door or control-state condition, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Check for Utility or Power Conditions Affecting the Door
steps.instructions: Verify that the sterilizer has stable electrical power and that facility utilities required for door operation are available. Do not assume the door actuator or internal mechanism has failed until external utility conditions are ruled out. Expected outcome: Required power and accessible utility conditions are normal. If restoration of an external utility restores door operation, perform functional verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Compare Behavior With an Unloaded Chamber
steps.instructions: If appropriate and safe, remove loading equipment and test door operation with an empty chamber. This helps distinguish a door-system problem from an interference problem caused by loading accessories. Expected outcome: The door closes, locks, and is recognized normally with the chamber empty. If so, correct the loading equipment or positioning issue before returning to use.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Cycle the door through normal opening, closing, and locking operations as permitted. Confirm the displayed door state agrees with actual position and that a cycle can be initiated only under appropriate safe conditions. Do not intentionally challenge or bypass safety interlocks. Expected outcome: Door operation is smooth, repeatable, and correctly recognized. If verified, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Door Problems
steps.instructions: If the door path, load position, external sealing surfaces, control sequence, opposite-door condition, power, and utilities are correct but the door still fails to close, lock, or register properly, stop troubleshooting. Likely service-level categories include door-position sensing, locking mechanism, actuator, alignment, interlock, or internal control problems. Expected outcome: The sterilizer remains out of production until the door system is properly evaluated and verified.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the AMSCO 600 Series chamber door would close physically but the sterilizer continued to indicate that the door was open.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose piece of packaging material trapped at the door edge, preventing complete closure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the obstruction, verified repeated door closure and recognition, initiated an approved test cycle, and confirmed normal operation.

helpfulDetails: Door side affected on pass-through units.

title: STERIS AMSCO 600 Series Sterilizer - Drain Temperature, Drain Blockage, or Chamber Drain Failure
description: Use this guide for abnormal drain temperature, slow drainage, standing chamber water, or cycle problems associated with the sterilizer drain path.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Safety and Avoid Hot-Water or Steam Exposure
steps.instructions: Do not reach into a hot chamber or drain area until the sterilizer is in a safe condition. Treat hot condensate, steam, and drain piping as burn hazards. Quarantine any load affected by a drain-related cycle failure. Expected outcome: Personnel are protected and no questionable processed load is released.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Drain Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether staff observed: Standing water in the chamber. Slow drainage. A drain-related alarm or message. Abnormally hot drain discharge. Cycle aborts associated with drainage. Water leaking externally. Problems limited to certain cycles. Record exact messages before clearing them. Expected outcome: The complaint is distinguished as blockage, drainage performance, temperature concern, leakage, or cycle-control behavior.

steps.title: 3. Allow the Chamber to Reach a Safe Condition
steps.instructions: Before inspecting the chamber drain, ensure the sterilizer is idle and the chamber is safe to access according to facility practice. Do not remove components from a pressurized or hot sterilizer. Expected outcome: The chamber can be inspected without exposure to pressure, steam, or unsafe heat.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Accessible Chamber Drain Area
steps.instructions: Visually inspect the chamber drain or strainer area for lint, labels, wrappers, tape, packaging fragments, or other accessible debris. Remove only debris that can be safely cleared without disassembling internal drain components. Expected outcome: The accessible drain path is clear. If removal of debris restores normal drainage, proceed to functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Check for Standing Water
steps.instructions: Observe whether water remains in the chamber after the unit should normally have drained. Document the amount and location qualitatively without inventing acceptable limits. Expected outcome: No abnormal standing water remains. Persistent accumulation suggests a deeper drain, valve, trap, or infrastructure issue.

steps.title: 6. Inspect External Drain Conditions
steps.instructions: Check accessible drain piping and the facility drain connection for obvious: Kinks or damage. Disconnection. Backup. Leakage. Recent plumbing work. Water accumulation around the sterilizer. Coordinate with Facilities if a building drain restriction is suspected. Expected outcome: The facility drain path appears open and intact. If an external plumbing restriction is found, correct or escalate the infrastructure problem before testing the sterilizer.

steps.title: 7. Check Relevant Facility Water Conditions
steps.instructions: Where applicable, verify that required water service associated with drain cooling or related sterilizer functions is available. Do not adjust undocumented valves or service settings. Expected outcome: Required external water service is present. An identified facility water interruption is corrected before further sterilizer testing.

steps.title: 8. Inspect for Abnormal Leakage or Heat
steps.instructions: Look for unexpected hot-water discharge, steam leakage, excessive condensation, or other evidence of uncontrolled thermal conditions. Do not attempt internal valve repair or place hands near suspected hot discharge points. Expected outcome: No unsafe external leakage or abnormal heat condition is present. Unsafe discharge requires removal from service.

steps.title: 9. Perform an Approved Functional Test
steps.instructions: After correcting any accessible blockage or infrastructure problem, run an approved test cycle and observe chamber drainage and cycle progression. Verify that water does not accumulate abnormally and that the cycle completes without a recurring drain-related condition. Expected outcome: Drainage is effective and repeatable and the sterilizer completes the appropriate test cycle. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Drain Failure
steps.instructions: If the accessible drain, external plumbing, utility conditions, and chamber condition are satisfactory but the problem persists, stop external troubleshooting. Possible service-level categories include internal drain valves, traps, temperature-control functions, cooling-water controls, sensors, plumbing, or control systems. Expected outcome: The sterilizer remains out of service until drain operation is properly evaluated and verified.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported standing water in the AMSCO 600 Series chamber and a cycle abort associated with drainage.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found packaging debris obstructing the accessible chamber drain area.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the debris, verified the chamber drained normally during an approved test cycle, confirmed successful cycle completion, and returned the sterilizer to service.

title: STERIS AMSCO 600 Series Sterilizer - Printer, Cycle Record, or Data Logging Failure
description: Use this guide when printed or electronic cycle records are missing, incomplete, unreadable, or unavailable despite otherwise normal sterilizer operation.

steps.title: 1. Protect Sterilization Documentation Integrity
steps.instructions: Do not allow a documentation problem to compromise load traceability or release practices. Follow facility policy when required cycle records are unavailable, incomplete, or unreadable. Do not recreate or falsify missing sterilization records. Expected outcome: Load release and recordkeeping remain compliant while the documentation issue is investigated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Documentation Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: No printed record. Blank or faint printing. Paper not feeding. Incomplete printout. Missing electronic record. Incorrect date/time information. Intermittent data logging. Loss of communication with an external documentation system. Expected outcome: The fault is narrowed to local printing, consumables, local data storage, configuration, or external communication.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Sterilizer Completed the Cycle
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the sterilizer itself completed the intended cycle normally. A missing printout does not prove that the cycle failed, and a successful printout does not prove sterilization performance by itself. Expected outcome: Cycle performance and documentation performance are treated as separate issues.

steps.title: 4. Check Printer Paper and Loading
steps.instructions: Inspect the printer for the correct paper presence and proper loading. Check for an empty roll, improperly routed paper, jam, or damaged leading edge. Use only appropriate facility-approved consumables. Expected outcome: Paper is present and feeds correctly. If correcting paper loading restores complete readable records, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Printer Area
steps.instructions: Check accessible printer surfaces, cover, feed path, and paper exit for debris or obstruction. Do not disassemble the printer mechanism beyond routine accessible areas. Expected outcome: The paper path is clear and the printer cover is properly secured.

steps.title: 6. Test Normal Print or Record Function
steps.instructions: Use normal user-accessible controls to generate an appropriate record or verify printing during an approved test cycle. Do not alter service configuration to force printer output. Expected outcome: A complete, legible record is produced. If so, verify repeatability and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 7. Verify Displayed Date and Time
steps.instructions: Check the sterilizer's displayed date and time against facility expectations. If incorrect, follow authorized facility procedures for adjustment. Do not enter restricted service menus or change validated configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The displayed date and time are correct or the discrepancy is documented for qualified configuration correction.

steps.title: 8. Check External Data Connections
steps.instructions: If cycle records are transmitted to another system, inspect accessible network, serial, or other communication cabling for secure connections and visible damage. Compare status with another known-good connection or port only when facility architecture and authorization permit. Expected outcome: External cabling and infrastructure appear intact. If reconnecting a loose accessible cable restores logging, verify successful transfer and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 9. Determine Whether the Fault Is Local or Network-Wide
steps.instructions: Check whether other sterilizers or devices using the same documentation platform are also unable to transmit records. Coordinate with IT, networking, or the appropriate integration support team when multiple devices are affected. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the sterilizer or identified as an infrastructure/system issue and routed appropriately.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Record Failure
steps.instructions: If consumables, paper path, normal controls, displayed time, accessible cabling, and infrastructure status are satisfactory but printing or data logging remains unreliable, stop external troubleshooting. Potential service-level categories include printer hardware, internal communication, storage, controller functions, configuration, or external integration software. Expected outcome: The documentation system is repaired or formally evaluated before routine use resumes where records are required.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the AMSCO 600 Series completed cycles but no printed cycle record was produced.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the printer paper roll empty.
CCR.Resolution: Installed the appropriate paper, verified proper paper feed and a complete legible record during an approved test cycle, and returned the sterilizer to service.

title: STERIS AMSCO 600 Series Sterilizer - Touchscreen, Control Panel, or Startup Failure
description: Use this guide when the sterilizer display, touchscreen, controls, or startup sequence is unavailable, frozen, unresponsive, or unreliable.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Safety and Processing Continuity
steps.instructions: Do not attempt to process a load on a sterilizer whose controls or display are unreliable. If a cycle is already active and the interface becomes abnormal, follow facility procedures and avoid actions that could compromise chamber safety. Move required processing to another verified sterilizer. Expected outcome: Clinical operations do not depend on an unreliable control system.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup or Control Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the sterilizer: Is completely dark. Powers on but does not complete startup. Displays a frozen screen. Responds to some controls but not others. Has an inaccurate or intermittently responsive touchscreen. Restarts unexpectedly. Displays a specific message. Record what is visible before restarting the unit. Expected outcome: The issue is defined as power loss, startup failure, display failure, touch-input failure, or intermittent control behavior.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility Electrical Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the sterilizer's expected facility electrical supply is available. Check for reported outages, tripped upstream infrastructure, or ongoing electrical work through appropriate facility channels. Do not repeatedly reset unexplained protective devices. Expected outcome: Stable facility power is available. If external power was lost, restore it through appropriate facility support before further evaluation.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible External Power and Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible cords, disconnects, connectors, and external control-panel connections where applicable for: Damage. Loose connections. Heat. Discoloration. Moisture. Physical impact. Do not open energized electrical enclosures for a basic startup complaint. Expected outcome: No obvious external electrical hazard or disconnected accessible connection is present. Damage, overheating, or moisture requires removal from service.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Touchscreen and Control Surface
steps.instructions: Check the screen and controls for: Liquid contamination. Cleaning residue. Protective film interference. Cracks. Impact damage. Objects contacting the screen. Gloves or environmental conditions interfering with normal touch response. Clean only according to approved facility/manufacturer methods. Expected outcome: The control surface is clean, dry, and physically intact. If contamination was causing false or missed touches and normal operation returns, proceed to verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Normal Control Response
steps.instructions: Using normal user controls only, check whether the display updates consistently and whether buttons or touchscreen selections correspond to the intended command. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or change configuration values. Expected outcome: Control inputs are accurate and repeatable. If the interface remains erratic, remove the unit from production use.

steps.title: 7. Perform an Approved Normal Restart
steps.instructions: If the sterilizer is idle and it is safe to do so, shut down and restart the unit using the normal approved procedure. Avoid cycling facility power repeatedly as a substitute for diagnosis. Expected outcome: The sterilizer completes startup and remains stable. If a single approved restart restores stable operation, continue with functional verification before deciding on return to service.

steps.title: 8. Observe for Repeatability
steps.instructions: Allow the sterilizer to remain powered and verify that the control panel does not freeze, reboot, blank, or begin generating unintended input. Intermittent control problems should not be dismissed solely because the screen works temporarily after restarting. Expected outcome: The interface remains stable and predictable. Any recurrence requires escalation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: With no production load at risk, verify normal cycle selection, door-status indication, control response, alarm/status display, and initiation of an approved test cycle. Confirm the display remains stable through the test. Expected outcome: Startup, controls, and display function reliably through normal operation. If all required checks pass without recurrence, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent or Intermittent Control Failure
steps.instructions: If facility power, accessible connections, touchscreen condition, normal restart, and control operation have been checked but the fault remains or recurs, stop external troubleshooting. Potential service-level categories include the display assembly, touchscreen interface, internal power supply, controller, communication, software, or configuration. Expected outcome: The sterilizer is removed from production until the control system is reliably repaired and verified.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the AMSCO 600 Series touchscreen powered on but did not respond reliably to selections.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried cleaning residue across the touchscreen surface causing inconsistent touch response.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned and dried the touchscreen using the approved method, verified accurate control response through repeated selections and an approved test cycle, and returned the sterilizer to service.

helpfulDetails: Blank, frozen, rebooting, or unresponsive condition.

title: STERIS AMSCO 600 Series Sterilizer - Vacuum Leak Test Failure
description: Use this guide when an approved vacuum leak test fails because of door sealing, chamber condition, drainage, moisture, or service-level vacuum faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Safety and Sterilization Reliability
steps.instructions: A failed vacuum leak test indicates the sterilizer may not reliably maintain the chamber conditions required for applicable cycles. Do not use the unit for production loads requiring verified air removal until the failure is resolved according to facility policy. Expected outcome: Questionable sterilization performance is prevented from affecting patient care.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Test Failure
steps.instructions: Review the test result and cycle record. Determine whether: The correct test cycle was selected. The chamber was empty as required by facility procedure. The test failed consistently or only once. A specific alarm or message accompanied the failure. The sterilizer had recently completed a hot or wet cycle. Do not invent or substitute acceptance limits; use the applicable manufacturer and facility criteria. Expected outcome: A genuine vacuum leak test failure is confirmed under appropriate test conditions.

steps.title: 3. Verify Chamber Is Empty and Properly Prepared
steps.instructions: Remove any load, packaging, loose materials, or accessories not intended to remain in the chamber during the test. Check that the chamber is in the appropriate condition for the approved leak-test procedure. Expected outcome: No load-related item can interfere with sealing or test conditions. If preparation error caused the result, repeat the test correctly and stop troubleshooting if it passes.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Door and Accessible Sealing Surfaces
steps.instructions: With the sterilizer safe, inspect the chamber opening and accessible sealing surfaces for: Debris. Packaging fragments. Tape or labels. Residue. Visible damage. Objects preventing complete closure. Do not remove or adjust internal door mechanisms. Expected outcome: The door closes fully against clean, unobstructed sealing surfaces. If cleaning or removing debris restores a passing test, complete required verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Verify Door Closure and Lock Recognition
steps.instructions: Operate the door normally and confirm the sterilizer recognizes the expected closed and locked condition. Do not bypass door sensing or locking interlocks. Expected outcome: The door locks normally and the control system consistently recognizes the correct state.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Chamber and Drain for Residual Water
steps.instructions: Look for abnormal standing water or excessive moisture in the chamber and inspect the accessible drain area for debris. Residual water or poor drainage may interfere with repeatable vacuum testing. Expected outcome: The chamber and drain appear normal with no obvious blockage or abnormal water accumulation. If an accessible obstruction is corrected, repeat the approved test.

steps.title: 7. Check for Obvious External Leakage
steps.instructions: Observe accessible door, drain, and utility areas for abnormal air, steam, or water leakage that may indicate a sealing problem. Do not disassemble vacuum piping or internal valves. Expected outcome: No obvious external leak is present. Any significant leak or damaged chamber/door hardware requires removal from service.

steps.title: 8. Allow Appropriate Stabilization Before Retesting
steps.instructions: If the previous cycle or chamber condition may have affected the test, follow facility and manufacturer procedures regarding preparation before repeating the test. Do not repeatedly run tests without addressing an identified cause. Expected outcome: The leak test is repeated under appropriate, consistent conditions.

steps.title: 9. Repeat the Approved Vacuum Leak Test
steps.instructions: Run the proper vacuum leak test using established facility and manufacturer criteria. Record the actual result. Expected outcome: The unit passes the approved leak test. If it passes and no other abnormal condition exists, troubleshooting can stop after all required return-to-service checks.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Repeated Leak-Test Failure
steps.instructions: If chamber preparation, door closure, sealing surfaces, drain condition, and external leakage have been checked and the approved test continues to fail, stop external troubleshooting. Potential service-level categories include internal valves, chamber plumbing, vacuum components, door sealing systems, drains, sensing, or control functions. Expected outcome: The sterilizer remains out of production until the vacuum system is properly evaluated.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the AMSCO 600 Series repeatedly failed its vacuum leak test.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a strip of packaging material on the chamber door sealing surface that prevented complete sealing.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the debris, cleaned the accessible sealing surface, repeated the approved vacuum leak test successfully, and verified the sterilizer was ready for service.

title: STERIS Reliance 444 Washer-Disinfector - Cycle Will Not Start, Aborts, or Stalls
description: Troubleshoots cycles that will not begin, stop unexpectedly, or remain in one phase because of power, doors, utilities, loading, or external conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Workflow and Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a washer-disinfector that cannot complete a validated cycle. Remove affected instruments from the normal processed workflow and follow facility procedures for alternative decontamination processing. Confirm whether the cycle: Will not start at all Starts and immediately aborts Stops consistently in the same phase Stalls intermittently Produces a visible message or alarm Record the selected cycle and the point where operation stops. Expected outcome: The failure mode and affected cycle phase are clearly identified. If the problem was an incorrect cycle selection or incomplete start sequence and the unit subsequently operates normally, verify a complete cycle and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Verify Power and Normal Startup
steps.instructions: Confirm the washer is powered, the display and controls respond normally, and no facility breaker, disconnect, or emergency power condition is affecting operation. Look for: Blank or resetting display Intermittent power Unusual startup behavior Signs of electrical overheating or damage Do not repeatedly reset a breaker or continue operating equipment with electrical damage. Expected outcome: Stable power and normal control operation are present. If restoring an external power condition corrects the problem and a complete verification cycle passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Check Door Position and Interlocks
steps.instructions: Verify all required doors are fully closed and unobstructed. Inspect visible door edges, seals, latching surfaces, and the load for anything preventing full closure. Do not bypass or defeat a door interlock. Expected outcome: The door closes normally and the system recognizes the required door state. If correcting an obstruction restores normal cycle operation, complete functional verification and stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify Rack, Cart, and Load Position
steps.instructions: Confirm the rack or processing cart is fully seated and properly aligned. Check that instruments, containers, hoses, or accessories are not interfering with chamber components, doors, spray arms, or manifold connections. Expected outcome: The load is correctly positioned without mechanical interference. If reseating or correcting the load allows the cycle to complete normally, stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Available Utilities
steps.instructions: Verify the washer has the facility utilities required for operation. Inspect accessible water, steam, air, drain, and other applicable service connections for obvious shutoff, leakage, disconnection, or facility outage conditions. Coordinate with Facilities when a utility issue is suspected. Expected outcome: Required utilities are available without obvious interruption. If an external utility issue is corrected and the washer completes a test cycle, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Check Chemistry Availability
steps.instructions: Confirm required detergent or other processing chemistry is present, correctly connected, and not visibly empty, kinked, disconnected, or leaking. Do not substitute unapproved chemistry. Expected outcome: Chemistry supply is available and externally connected correctly. If restoring the chemistry supply allows normal operation, verify the completed cycle and stop.

steps.title: 7. Compare Cycle Behavior
steps.instructions: If permitted by facility procedure, perform an unloaded or approved test cycle and observe whether the unit progresses normally. Determine whether the problem: Occurs on all cycles Occurs on one cycle only Occurs only with a particular rack or load type Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to the washer, a cycle configuration, or an external loading condition. A successful repeat cycle after correcting an external cause resolves the issue.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After any correction, run the appropriate verification cycle according to facility and manufacturer requirements. Confirm normal filling, washing, draining, temperature progression, door operation, chemistry delivery, and cycle completion as applicable. Expected outcome: The cycle completes without alarms or abnormal interruption and required cycle documentation is produced. The washer may be returned to service only when all required checks pass.

steps.title: 9. Escalate if the Cycle Still Aborts or Stalls
steps.instructions: If power, doors, loading, rack position, utilities, and chemistry have been ruled out, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: An unresolved washer is removed from service rather than repeatedly cycled or returned to clinical processing.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance 444 started a cycle but repeatedly stopped before completion.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the processing rack was not fully seated and was interfering with normal cycle initiation.
CCR.Resolution: Rack position was corrected, the washer completed a full verification cycle without interruption, and the unit was returned to service.

title: STERIS Reliance 444 Washer-Disinfector - Chamber Will Not Fill or Water Level Is Incorrect
description: Troubleshoots absent, slow, excessive, or inconsistent chamber filling caused by water supply, loading, drainage, or other external conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing and Confirm the Fill Problem
steps.instructions: Do not use the washer for instrument processing when chamber filling is unreliable. Identify whether the chamber: Does not fill Fills slowly Appears underfilled Appears overfilled Produces inconsistent water levels between cycles Record the cycle and phase where the condition occurs. Expected outcome: The exact fill complaint is confirmed. If the observation was related to normal cycle behavior and a complete verified cycle operates normally, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 2. Verify Normal Power and Cycle Initiation
steps.instructions: Confirm the washer remains powered and is actually progressing into a fill phase rather than being held by another condition such as an open door or incomplete rack connection. Expected outcome: The unit is stable and is commanding normal cycle progression. If correcting an external start condition restores filling, verify the cycle and stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility Water Availability
steps.instructions: Check accessible incoming water services for: Closed isolation valves Facility water interruption Obvious supply leakage Recent plumbing work Abnormally low water availability elsewhere in the department Coordinate with Facilities if supply pressure or infrastructure is suspected. Expected outcome: Required facility water supplies are available. If an external supply condition is corrected and normal fill is restored, complete a verification cycle and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Supply Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect visible hoses, fittings, strainers or accessible connection areas without disassembly for kinks, crushing, leakage, or obstruction. Do not open pressurized plumbing or internal valves unless qualified and authorized. Expected outcome: External supply connections are intact and unobstructed. Correcting a visible external restriction should restore normal filling.

steps.title: 5. Check the Chamber and Load
steps.instructions: Inspect the chamber for misplaced items, packaging, containers, or debris that could interfere with visible level sensing areas, drains, or water distribution. Verify the rack and load are correctly positioned. Expected outcome: Nothing in the chamber or load is interfering with normal filling or drainage. If removing an obstruction corrects the water level, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 6. Check for Simultaneous Drainage
steps.instructions: Observe whether incoming water appears to leave the chamber unusually quickly. A drain condition can appear to be a fill problem. Inspect accessible drain areas for obvious blockage or abnormal flow. Expected outcome: The chamber retains water appropriately during the required portion of the cycle. If a simple accessible drain obstruction caused the symptom and is safely corrected, verify the cycle and stop.

steps.title: 7. Compare Repeated Cycle Behavior
steps.instructions: Run an approved verification cycle and determine whether the fill problem occurs: Every cycle Only after a previous cycle Only with one rack or load configuration Intermittently Expected outcome: The failure pattern is defined. If repeated cycles fill consistently after correcting an external cause, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the chamber fills and drains normally throughout the verification cycle without leakage, overfill, or interruption. Expected outcome: Normal cycle progression is restored and the washer completes its required verification. The unit may be returned to service only after successful testing.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Unresolved Fill Problems
steps.instructions: If water supply, visible connections, loading, and drainage conditions are normal but fill remains incorrect, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The washer is removed from service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance 444 chamber was not filling adequately during the wash cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the facility water isolation valve supplying the washer was partially closed.
CCR.Resolution: Facilities restored the valve to its proper position, and Clinical Engineering verified normal chamber filling and a complete successful cycle.

helpfulDetails: Whether fill was absent, slow, low, or excessive

title: STERIS Reliance 444 Washer-Disinfector - Wash Temperature or Thermal Rinse Temperature Not Reached
description: Troubleshoots cycles that fail to reach required heating stages because of utility availability, loading, water conditions, or service-level temperature problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing and Confirm the Temperature Failure
steps.instructions: Do not release instruments from a cycle that failed its required temperature phase. Follow facility procedures for reprocessing the affected load. Confirm: Which cycle was selected Whether wash temperature, thermal rinse temperature, or both were affected Whether the cycle aborted or continued Any displayed alarm or message Expected outcome: The temperature failure and affected cycle stage are clearly identified.

steps.title: 2. Verify Stable Power and Normal Cycle Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the washer remains powered and progresses normally through filling and circulation before the heating problem occurs. Expected outcome: The unit has stable electrical power and reaches the expected heating phase. If a power interruption caused the failure and a repeat cycle completes normally after correction, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Required Facility Utilities
steps.instructions: Check accessible utility conditions relevant to heating. Look for: Closed utility isolation valves Recent steam or hot-water outage Facility maintenance Other nearby equipment reporting similar utility problems Visible leakage Coordinate with Facilities for infrastructure verification when needed. Expected outcome: Heating-related facility utilities are available. If an external utility outage is corrected and temperatures are subsequently achieved, verify the cycle and stop.

steps.title: 4. Confirm Normal Chamber Filling
steps.instructions: Verify the washer is filling normally. Incorrect water level can affect heat-up performance. Expected outcome: Chamber filling appears normal without obvious underfill, overfill, or continuous draining. If correcting a fill problem restores normal temperatures, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Load and Rack Configuration
steps.instructions: Check for overloading, tightly nested items, improper rack use, or load placement that could interfere with circulation. Expected outcome: The washer contains an appropriate, correctly positioned load. If correcting the load allows the cycle to reach temperature and complete normally, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Review Cycle Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm the expected temperature stage actually belongs to the selected authorized cycle. Do not change validated cycle programming or temperature configuration without proper authorization. Expected outcome: The correct cycle has been selected. If an incorrect cycle selection caused the complaint, verify operation using the intended approved cycle and stop.

steps.title: 7. Compare the Displayed Temperature Trend
steps.instructions: During an approved verification cycle, observe whether temperature: Rises normally but stops short Rises unusually slowly Remains unchanged Behaves erratically Do not assume the internal temperature display is accurate if performance is questionable. Expected outcome: The temperature behavior is characterized for escalation or confirmation.

steps.title: 8. Perform Approved Temperature Verification
steps.instructions: When within Clinical Engineering responsibility, use appropriate approved test equipment and manufacturer procedures to verify heating performance. Do not adjust calibration or temperature configuration unless authorized and qualified. Expected outcome: Measured performance agrees with acceptable manufacturer or facility requirements. If verification passes consistently, the washer may be returned to service.

steps.title: 9. Escalate if Required Temperature Cannot Be Verified
steps.instructions: If utilities, water level, loading, and cycle selection are correct but required temperatures are not reached, remove the washer from service. Expected outcome: A washer with unverified thermal performance is not used for clinical processing.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance 444 repeatedly failed to reach the expected thermal rinse temperature.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering confirmed a facility steam interruption was preventing normal heating during the cycle.
CCR.Resolution: Facilities restored the utility supply, and Clinical Engineering verified that the washer completed a full cycle with normal temperature progression.

title: STERIS Reliance 444 Washer-Disinfector - Door Will Not Lock, Unlock, or Seal
description: Troubleshoots door locking, unlocking, closure, and sealing problems caused by obstructions, alignment, loading, contamination, or external control conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Personnel and Confirm the Door Condition
steps.instructions: Do not force a washer door open or defeat a door interlock. If the chamber may be hot, pressurized, or contain hot water or chemistry, keep personnel clear and allow the machine to reach a safe state. Determine whether the door: Will not close Closes but will not lock Remains locked after cycle completion Leaks at the seal Is physically difficult to move Expected outcome: The exact door problem is safely identified.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Cycle Status
steps.instructions: Verify whether the washer is: Idle In an active cycle Completing a drain or cool-down stage Reporting an alarm or incomplete cycle A door remaining locked during an unsafe process condition may be normal protective behavior. Expected outcome: The door condition is evaluated in relation to the washer's current cycle state. If normal cycle completion releases the door as intended, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Load Obstruction
steps.instructions: Check whether a rack, instrument, tray, hose, packaging material, or other object is preventing full closure. Expected outcome: The door path is clear. If removing the obstruction restores normal closure and locking, verify operation and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Door Seal and Contact Surfaces
steps.instructions: Visually inspect accessible sealing surfaces for: Debris Residue Damage Folding or displacement Foreign material Clean only according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: Sealing surfaces are clean and visibly intact. If approved cleaning restores a proper seal, verify a full cycle and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Door Alignment and Movement
steps.instructions: Without forcing the mechanism, observe whether the door moves smoothly and appears normally aligned. Look for visible: Sagging Impact damage Loose external hardware Binding Expected outcome: Door movement is smooth with no obvious mechanical damage. Visible structural damage requires removal from service.

steps.title: 6. Verify Power and Control Response
steps.instructions: Confirm stable power and normal control-panel response. An incomplete power or control state may prevent normal lock or unlock operation. Expected outcome: Controls are responsive and the washer recognizes the correct cycle status.

steps.title: 7. Check for Leakage During an Approved Test
steps.instructions: If the door closes and locks normally, perform an approved verification cycle and observe the perimeter for leakage from a safe distance. Do not continue testing if leakage becomes significant. Expected outcome: The door remains securely closed and dry throughout the cycle. If leakage is absent and operation is normal, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify normal door closure, locking, cycle operation, unlocking, and sealing during a complete approved test cycle. Expected outcome: Door operation is repeatable and safe. Only then should the unit be returned to service.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Unresolved Door Problems
steps.instructions: If the door will not lock, unlock, align, or seal after external causes are ruled out, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The washer is removed from service rather than operated with an unreliable safety barrier.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance 444 door would close but would not lock for a cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a tray handle protruding from the rack and preventing full door closure.
CCR.Resolution: The load was repositioned, and normal door locking, sealing, cycle completion, and unlocking were verified.

title: STERIS Reliance 444 Washer-Disinfector - Detergent or Chemistry Is Not Dispensing
description: Troubleshoots missing or inconsistent chemistry delivery caused by empty containers, tubing problems, incorrect connections, loading conditions, or service-level dispensing faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing and Confirm the Complaint
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a cycle with unverified chemistry delivery. Follow facility procedures for any load processed during a suspected detergent or chemistry failure. Confirm whether: Chemistry was not consumed A low-chemistry condition was reported The cycle aborted Dispensing appears intermittent One chemistry channel or multiple channels are affected Expected outcome: The affected chemistry and failure pattern are identified.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Correct Chemistry Is Available
steps.instructions: Confirm the required approved chemistry container is present and contains sufficient product. Check the product identification according to facility practice. Do not substitute chemicals based only on container fit. Expected outcome: The correct approved chemistry is available. If replacing an empty approved container restores normal operation, verify dispensing and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 3. Inspect External Pickup Tubing
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible chemistry tubing for: Kinks Pinching Disconnection Cracks Air gaps Incorrect routing Tubing not fully inserted into the intended container Wear appropriate PPE and avoid direct chemical contact. Expected outcome: External tubing is intact and properly routed. If correcting an external tubing problem restores dispensing, complete verification and stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Correct Container Connection
steps.instructions: Confirm each pickup tube is connected to the intended chemistry and has not been swapped during container replacement or housekeeping. Expected outcome: Each chemistry connection matches its intended supply. If correcting the connection resolves the problem, verify the next approved cycle.

steps.title: 5. Inspect for Leakage
steps.instructions: Look for visible chemical leakage around the container, tubing, floor, and accessible connection points. Do not operate the washer with an active chemical leak. Expected outcome: No external chemistry leakage is present. Leakage that cannot be corrected externally requires removal from service.

steps.title: 6. Confirm Cycle Selection
steps.instructions: Verify the selected cycle is one that normally uses the chemistry in question. Do not alter validated cycle chemistry settings without authorization. Expected outcome: The selected cycle appropriately calls for the required chemistry.

steps.title: 7. Observe Chemistry Consumption During Verification
steps.instructions: When permitted, mark or otherwise document the starting chemistry level and run an approved verification cycle. Do not infer correct dosing solely from a slight change in container level when precise verification is required. Expected outcome: Chemistry delivery is confirmed according to approved manufacturer or facility verification procedures.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify the washer completes the intended cycle without chemistry-related alarms and that required dispensing checks pass. Expected outcome: Correct chemistry delivery and cycle completion are demonstrated. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate if Dispensing Remains Unverified
steps.instructions: If the correct chemistry is available and external tubing and connections are normal but delivery remains absent or inconsistent, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The washer is removed from service pending qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance 444 was completing cycles but detergent did not appear to be dispensing.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the detergent pickup tube kinked behind the chemistry container.
CCR.Resolution: The tubing was repositioned, correct chemistry delivery was verified during an approved test cycle, and the washer was returned to service.

title: STERIS Reliance 444 Washer-Disinfector - Spray Arm Does Not Rotate or Wash Pressure Is Low
description: Troubleshoots poor spray action or circulation caused by loading, blocked spray components, rack connections, water supply, or service-level circulation problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing and Confirm the Condition
steps.instructions: Do not release a load if adequate washing action is in doubt. Identify whether: One spray arm appears affected Multiple spray arms are affected Wash pressure is reported low Cleaning results are poor The problem occurs with one rack or all racks Expected outcome: The circulation complaint is clearly defined.

steps.title: 2. Inspect the Load for Mechanical Interference
steps.instructions: Check whether instruments, trays, containers, hoses, or other items physically block spray-arm movement. Manually check accessible spray-arm freedom only when the washer is safely stopped and according to approved handling procedures. Expected outcome: Spray arms have unobstructed movement. If repositioning the load restores normal operation, verify a complete cycle and stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Accessible Spray Openings
steps.instructions: Check accessible spray holes and surfaces for visible debris, labels, tape, scale, or other obstruction. Perform only approved routine cleaning. Expected outcome: Accessible spray openings are clear. If approved cleaning restores circulation, verify performance and stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify Rack and Manifold Seating
steps.instructions: Confirm the rack or cart is fully inserted and correctly engaged with the washer's water connection or manifold interface. Look for: Misalignment Damaged visible seals Incomplete insertion Obstruction at the connection Expected outcome: The rack connection is secure and properly aligned. If reseating the rack restores spray performance, complete verification and stop.

steps.title: 5. Compare With a Known-Good Rack
steps.instructions: If another compatible verified rack is available, compare operation. Do not use a damaged or unverified rack as the comparison. Expected outcome: If the problem follows one rack, investigate that rack or its manifold externally. If the problem remains with multiple racks, the washer itself becomes more suspect.

steps.title: 6. Verify Normal Chamber Fill
steps.instructions: Confirm the washer is filling normally. Insufficient water can reduce effective circulation. Expected outcome: Chamber water level appears normal for the cycle. If a corrected fill problem restores wash action, stop after successful verification.

steps.title: 7. Check for External Utility Problems
steps.instructions: Verify required water services are available and no facility condition is affecting supply. Expected outcome: External water supply is normal.

steps.title: 8. Perform an Approved Verification Cycle
steps.instructions: Run an approved test using a correctly seated rack and proper load configuration. Observe for normal cycle progression and any available wash-pressure indication or alarm. Expected outcome: Spray action and circulation remain stable through the wash phase. If performance is normal, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Low-Pressure Conditions
steps.instructions: If spray paths, loading, rack connection, fill, and utilities are normal but circulation remains weak, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The washer is removed from service for further evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported poor cleaning results and observed that the upper spray arm on the Reliance 444 was not rotating.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a large tray positioned high enough to obstruct spray-arm movement.
CCR.Resolution: The tray was repositioned, unrestricted spray-arm movement and normal cycle operation were verified, and the washer was returned to service.

title: STERIS Reliance 444 Washer-Disinfector - Drain Is Slow, Blocked, or Leaves Water in Chamber
description: Troubleshoots slow or incomplete drainage caused by visible debris, load obstruction, drain infrastructure, or service-level drainage problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Personnel and Confirm the Drain Problem
steps.instructions: Do not reach into retained chamber water until temperature and chemical hazards are known and the unit is in a safe state. Determine whether: Water drains slowly Water remains after cycle completion Drainage stops completely The chamber refills unexpectedly The cycle aborts during a drain phase Expected outcome: The drainage problem is clearly characterized.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Cycle Has Actually Reached Drain
steps.instructions: Confirm the washer is not intentionally retaining water as part of the selected cycle stage. Expected outcome: The reported retained water is confirmed to be abnormal. If the condition is normal cycle behavior, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Chamber for Debris
steps.instructions: When safe and permitted, inspect accessible chamber and drain-screen areas for: Labels Packaging Instrument debris Broken components Excess residue Remove only accessible debris according to approved cleaning procedures. Expected outcome: Accessible drain paths are clear. If removing debris restores normal draining, verify a full cycle and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check Load Position
steps.instructions: Verify trays, racks, containers, and accessories are not obstructing the chamber drain area. Expected outcome: The load does not interfere with drainage.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Drain Connections
steps.instructions: Look for visible: Kinked drain hoses Crushed tubing Leakage Improper routing Obvious external blockage Do not disconnect hot or chemically contaminated drain lines unless authorized and protected. Expected outcome: External drain connections appear unobstructed and intact.

steps.title: 6. Evaluate Facility Drain Performance
steps.instructions: Determine whether nearby sinks, washers, or floor drains show similar slow drainage. Coordinate with Facilities when building drainage is suspected. Expected outcome: Facility drainage is functioning normally. If Facilities corrects an infrastructure blockage and washer drainage returns to normal, verify the cycle and stop.

steps.title: 7. Compare Loaded and Unloaded Operation
steps.instructions: If appropriate, perform an approved test cycle without the suspect load or rack. Expected outcome: If drainage is normal without the load, the issue may be load or rack related. If drainage remains abnormal, the washer or facility drain requires further evaluation.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Run an approved verification cycle and confirm the chamber drains completely at the appropriate phases without backup or leakage. Expected outcome: Normal drainage and cycle completion are demonstrated. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Drainage Problems
steps.instructions: If visible debris, load position, external connections, and facility drainage have been ruled out, remove the washer from service. Expected outcome: An unresolved drainage problem is referred for qualified service.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported standing water remained in the Reliance 444 chamber after cycles completed.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found disposable label material obstructing the accessible chamber drain screen.
CCR.Resolution: The debris was removed using approved procedures, and a complete verification cycle confirmed normal drainage with no residual chamber water.

helpfulDetails: Amount or location of retained water

title: STERIS Reliance 444 Washer-Disinfector - Rack, Manifold, or Cart Connection Not Detected
description: Troubleshoots rack or cart recognition problems caused by poor seating, alignment, damaged connections, contamination, or incompatible processing accessories.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing and Confirm the Detection Problem
steps.instructions: Do not process a load if the washer cannot reliably recognize or connect to the required rack, manifold, or cart. Confirm whether: The washer refuses to start The rack is physically seated but not recognized Detection is intermittent Only one rack is affected A water-manifold connection does not engage Expected outcome: The affected rack or connection and the exact symptom are identified.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Correct Rack or Cart Is Being Used
steps.instructions: Confirm the rack, manifold, or cart is appropriate for the washer and intended cycle. Do not modify or force incompatible accessories into position. Expected outcome: The correct compatible processing accessory is present.

steps.title: 3. Fully Remove and Reseat the Rack
steps.instructions: With the washer in a safe idle condition, remove the rack or cart and reinstall it carefully. Check for: Incomplete insertion Skewed wheels Objects on guide tracks Load overhang Resistance before full seating Expected outcome: The rack reaches its normal fully seated position. If reseating restores detection, perform a verification cycle and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Rack Connection Area
steps.instructions: Visually inspect accessible manifold interfaces, alignment features, seals, and connection surfaces for: Debris Damage Bent external parts Missing visible components Heavy residue Do not disassemble the internal connection mechanism. Expected outcome: Connection surfaces are clean, intact, and aligned.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Load for Interference
steps.instructions: Confirm instruments or trays are not preventing the rack from reaching its final seated position. Expected outcome: The load does not interfere with rack insertion or connection.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good Rack
steps.instructions: If available, test another compatible verified rack or cart. Expected outcome: If the known-good rack is detected, the original rack or manifold is isolated as the likely source. If no compatible rack is detected, the washer requires further evaluation.

steps.title: 7. Check for Reproducibility
steps.instructions: Repeat insertion several times only if safe and appropriate. Determine whether detection is consistent or dependent on rack position. Expected outcome: A properly functioning system recognizes the rack consistently. Intermittent recognition should not be accepted for clinical processing.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting an external issue, run the appropriate cycle with the rack fully connected and verify normal filling, circulation, cycle completion, and rack recognition. Expected outcome: Rack detection remains stable throughout the cycle. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Detection Problems
steps.instructions: If correct rack type, seating, alignment, cleanliness, and known-good comparison have been addressed and detection remains unreliable, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The washer or affected rack is removed from service as appropriate.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance 444 would not recognize one processing rack and would not begin the cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found debris on the rack guide preventing the rack from reaching its fully seated position.
CCR.Resolution: The obstruction was removed, repeatable rack detection and normal manifold engagement were verified, and the washer completed a successful test cycle.

helpfulDetails: Whether one or all racks are affected

title: STERIS Reliance 444 Washer-Disinfector - Printer, Cycle Record, or Data Export Failure
description: Troubleshoots missing cycle documentation, printer problems, or export failures caused by supplies, connections, destination availability, configuration, or communication issues.

steps.title: 1. Protect Documentation Integrity and Confirm the Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The printer produces no output Print is blank or incomplete The cycle record is missing Stored cycle data cannot be retrieved Export to an external system fails Do not recreate or alter processing records in a way that could misrepresent cycle completion. Expected outcome: The documentation failure is clearly identified while preserving record integrity.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Cycle Completed Normally
steps.instructions: Confirm the underlying washer cycle completed successfully and the issue is limited to documentation or data transfer. Expected outcome: The washer's processing function is separated from the record-output problem. If the cycle itself failed, troubleshoot the cycle failure instead.

steps.title: 3. Check Printer Supplies and Physical Condition
steps.instructions: For an attached printer, inspect: Paper supply Paper loading Cover closure Visible jams External damage Printer power or indicators Use only the approved consumable type. Expected outcome: Printer supplies and physical setup are correct. If replacing or properly loading consumables restores printing, verify a test record and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Cables and Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible printer, network, serial, USB, or other applicable external data connections for: Loose plugs Damaged connectors Disconnected cables Strain or pinching Expected outcome: External communication connections are secure and undamaged.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Intended Output Destination
steps.instructions: Confirm the printer, export destination, or connected documentation system is available and not offline. For networked systems, coordinate with IT when the destination server, network port, interface, or application may be unavailable. Expected outcome: The external destination is reachable and available. If restoring an external system corrects the failure, verify successful transfer and stop.

steps.title: 6. Confirm Authorized Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify visible user-accessible output settings are appropriate. Do not alter protected configuration, network parameters, or service settings without authorization. Expected outcome: Approved output configuration appears correct.

steps.title: 7. Test With a New Completed Cycle
steps.instructions: Run an approved test cycle if required and confirm a new cycle record is generated, printed, stored, or exported successfully. Expected outcome: Complete documentation is produced and associated with the correct test cycle. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Verify Historical Data Carefully
steps.instructions: If historical cycle records are involved, avoid deleting, overwriting, or modifying existing records during troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Existing records remain preserved while current functionality is tested.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Documentation Failures
steps.instructions: If supplies, external connections, destination availability, and authorized settings are correct but records remain unavailable, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The documentation subsystem is referred for qualified service or IT evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance 444 completed cycles but no printed cycle record was produced.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the printer paper roll empty with no additional printer fault present.
CCR.Resolution: Approved printer paper was installed, and a subsequent test cycle produced a complete and legible cycle record.

helpfulDetails: Whether print, storage, or export failed

title: STERIS Reliance 444 Washer-Disinfector - Repeated Leak, Overfill, or Water-on-Floor Condition
description: Troubleshoots visible leaks, chamber overfill, or water on the floor caused by doors, hoses, drains, loading, utilities, or service-level plumbing problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Personnel and Remove the Washer From Use
steps.instructions: Stop using the washer if active leakage, overfill, or water on the floor creates a slip, electrical, burn, or chemical hazard. Keep staff clear of the affected area and follow facility procedures for spill control. If water is approaching electrical equipment or power connections, do not touch wet electrical components. Expected outcome: The area is safe and the washer is no longer being used while the leak source is unknown.

steps.title: 2. Identify When the Leak Occurs
steps.instructions: Determine whether water appears during: Filling Washing Draining Thermal rinse Door opening Idle periods Note the approximate location where water first becomes visible. Expected outcome: The leak is associated with a cycle phase and general area, narrowing the likely external causes.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Door and Seal Area
steps.instructions: Check for: Debris on the sealing surface Load interference Visible seal damage Water tracking from the door perimeter Incomplete closure Do not continue cycling a washer with a visibly damaged seal or unreliable lock. Expected outcome: The door seals normally without visible obstruction. If an external obstruction is corrected and no leakage recurs during verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Water Connections
steps.instructions: Visually inspect accessible hoses, fittings, supply lines, and connections for: Drips Loose external connections Cracks Kinks Signs of recent movement Do not tighten or disconnect pressurized connections unless qualified and authorized. Expected outcome: No external water supply leak is present.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Drain Connections and Floor Drain Area
steps.instructions: Look for: Drain backup Disconnected or damaged drain hose Water overflowing from a floor drain Slow building drainage Coordinate with Facilities if the water source may be infrastructure rather than the washer itself. Expected outcome: Facility drains and accessible washer drain connections are functioning normally. If Facilities resolves a drain backup and the washer remains dry during testing, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Check the Chamber for Overfill
steps.instructions: If safe, determine whether the chamber contains an abnormal amount of water before the leak occurs. Do not continue running repeated cycles to observe an active overfill condition. Expected outcome: Normal chamber fill is distinguished from a true overfill. A confirmed overfill requires service evaluation if no simple external cause is present.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Rack and Load Position
steps.instructions: Verify nothing in the load is directing spray toward the door, blocking drainage, preventing closure, or interfering with internal water distribution. Expected outcome: The rack and load are correctly positioned. If correcting the load eliminates leakage, complete a verification cycle and stop.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Verification Only if Safe
steps.instructions: If the visible cause has been corrected and there is no electrical or chemical hazard, perform an approved test cycle while observing from a safe location. Stop the cycle if leakage recurs. Expected outcome: The complete cycle runs without leakage, overfill, or water accumulation on the floor. Only then may troubleshooting stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Repeated or Unexplained Leakage
steps.instructions: If the source is internal, leakage recurs, overfill continues, or the source cannot be safely identified, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The washer remains out of service pending qualified repair.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported water collecting on the floor in front of the Reliance 444 during wash cycles.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found debris on the lower door sealing surface preventing the door from sealing completely.
CCR.Resolution: The sealing surface was cleaned using the approved procedure, and a full verification cycle completed with no leakage or water accumulation.

title: STERIS SYSTEM 1E Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Troubleshoots loss of power, incomplete startup, failed initialization, external power problems, connection issues, and conditions preventing the SYSTEM 1E from becoming ready.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Reprocessing Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a SYSTEM 1E that cannot complete startup for processing devices needed for patient care. Move reprocessing to another validated unit or approved workflow according to facility policy. Do not consider any interrupted or questionable load processed. Expected outcome: Clinical operations continue using an approved alternative while the affected unit is evaluated. If another verified unit restores workflow, continue troubleshooting the SYSTEM 1E offline.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Ask staff whether the unit is completely dead, powers on briefly, stops during initialization, freezes at a startup screen, restarts repeatedly, or displays a specific message. Determine whether the problem followed a power interruption, cleaning, relocation, service activity, or utility event. Expected outcome: The failure is reproduced or clearly characterized. If the unit now completes startup normally, perform additional startup cycles and functional verification before returning it to service.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Immediate Safety Concerns
steps.instructions: Check for liquid around the unit, unusual odor, overheating, damaged cords, damaged plugs, loose panels, visible leakage, or signs of electrical damage. Do not energize equipment with obvious electrical or water-related hazards. Expected outcome: No unsafe physical condition is present. If damage, leakage, overheating, or electrical hazard is found, remove the unit from service and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Verify Facility Power
steps.instructions: Confirm that the unit is connected to its intended power source. Inspect the plug and accessible cord for damage or looseness. Verify the receptacle using an approved tester or known-good device when permitted by facility procedure. Check for a tripped facility breaker or switched receptacle only within Clinical Engineering's authorized scope. Expected outcome: Stable facility power is available at the equipment connection. If restoring the power source allows normal startup, verify repeated operation and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Accessible Power Controls and Connections
steps.instructions: Verify that accessible power switches, emergency shutoffs, disconnects, or related external controls are in their normal operating position. Confirm accessible external connectors have not been disturbed. Expected outcome: Required external controls and connections are correctly positioned. If correcting an external connection restores startup, repeat startup and confirm normal readiness before stopping.

steps.title: 6. Perform a Controlled Power Cycle
steps.instructions: If the equipment is safe to operate and no load is being processed, shut the unit down using the normal method when possible. Allow shutdown to complete, then restore power and observe the full startup sequence. Do not repeatedly cycle power if the unit continually resets or shows signs of hardware instability. Expected outcome: The SYSTEM 1E completes initialization and reaches its normal ready state. If it does, perform functional verification and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Check Utility Availability Affecting Initialization
steps.instructions: Confirm required facility utilities serving the reprocessor are available and that accessible supply valves have not been closed. A unit may energize but remain unavailable if required water, drain, or other infrastructure conditions are not satisfied. Expected outcome: Required facility utilities are available and no obvious external utility issue is preventing readiness. If restoring a utility allows startup to complete, verify normal operation and stop.

steps.title: 8. Review Observable Messages and Indicators
steps.instructions: Record any startup message, alarm text, indicator status, or point in the startup sequence where progress stops. Do not clear configuration, enter unauthorized service modes, or repeatedly acknowledge unexplained faults simply to place the unit into service. Expected outcome: Any remaining startup failure is documented accurately enough for service escalation. If the message clears after correction of an identified external cause and the unit starts normally, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After a correction, restart the unit again and confirm normal display operation, controls, utility readiness, door operation, and absence of abnormal alarms or leakage. Conduct any required return-to-service testing according to facility and manufacturer procedures.
