Expected outcome: The SYSTEM 1E starts consistently and is ready for normal processing without abnormal indications. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If reliable facility power, accessible connections, controls, and utilities are verified but startup still fails, stop external troubleshooting. Do not perform board-level repair or unauthorized internal adjustments. Expected outcome: The unit is removed from clinical use and routed for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the STERIS SYSTEM 1E would not complete startup and remained unavailable for processing.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the unit connected to a facility receptacle that was not supplying power.
CCR.Resolution: Restored connection to a verified powered receptacle, confirmed repeated normal startup, and completed functional verification before returning the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the unit was completely dead or stopped during startup

title: STERIS SYSTEM 1E Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Cycle Will Not Start, Aborts, or Stalls
description: Troubleshoots cycles that will not begin, stop unexpectedly, or remain in one phase because of loading, utility, consumable, door, or external conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Load and Maintain Reprocessing Continuity
steps.instructions: Treat any cycle that did not complete normally as unsuccessful unless facility and manufacturer procedures explicitly establish otherwise. Do not release affected devices for patient use. Transfer processing to another validated system if needed. Expected outcome: Potentially incompletely processed devices remain segregated and clinical workflow continues safely. Troubleshoot the affected SYSTEM 1E without relying on it for patient-ready devices.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Where the Cycle Fails
steps.instructions: Ask whether the cycle never starts, aborts immediately, stops during filling, processing, draining, or another phase, or appears frozen. Record displayed messages and determine whether the same condition occurs with repeated attempts. Expected outcome: The failure point is identified. If the cycle subsequently completes normally, investigate the original cause and perform another controlled verification before stopping.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Unit and Processing Area
steps.instructions: Check for leakage, water on the floor, unusual noise, odor, overheating, loose accessories, damaged external components, or an improperly seated load. Stop immediately if a safety hazard is present. Expected outcome: No physical hazard exists. If leakage, overheating, or damage is found, remove the equipment from service rather than continuing cycle attempts.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Door Is Fully Closed and Ready
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible door, seal, latch, and load-area surfaces for obstruction, debris, or improperly positioned items. Confirm nothing in the load interferes with closure or locking. Expected outcome: The door closes normally and the system recognizes the required safe condition. If correcting an obstruction allows the cycle to start and complete, verify operation and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Load and Accessories Are Properly Positioned
steps.instructions: Confirm the load, processing tray, connectors, tubing, adapters, and other required accessories are installed and routed correctly according to approved processing practice. Look for pinched, disconnected, or visibly damaged external components. Expected outcome: The load and all required external accessories are correctly installed. If correcting setup restores a complete cycle, stop after final verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Required Consumables
steps.instructions: Confirm required chemistry or other cycle consumables are present, correctly installed, within permitted use conditions, and not visibly damaged. Do not bypass consumable recognition or substitute unapproved materials. Expected outcome: Required consumables are available and accepted by the system. If replacement of an exhausted or incorrectly installed consumable restores normal operation, verify a complete cycle and stop.

steps.title: 7. Check Facility Utilities
steps.instructions: Verify required water, drain, electrical power, and other facility services are available. Look for closed accessible valves, kinked external hoses, blocked visible drains, or evidence of a building utility problem. Expected outcome: External utilities are available and unrestricted. If correcting a utility problem allows the cycle to complete normally, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 8. Observe a Controlled Test Cycle
steps.instructions: With the unit safe to operate and using an approved test setup, initiate a cycle and observe whether it progresses normally. Note exactly where any delay or abort occurs. Do not repeatedly run failed cycles without determining why. Expected outcome: The cycle proceeds through its expected phases without unexplained interruption. If successful, perform final verification and document the correction.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm normal cycle initiation, progression, completion indication, drainage, door release, and cycle documentation as applicable. Verify no abnormal alarms or leakage occurred. Expected outcome: A complete cycle finishes normally and the unit is ready for service. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Repeated Cycle Failure
steps.instructions: If load setup, consumables, door condition, and facility utilities are correct but the unit repeatedly aborts or stalls, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The system is removed from service and referred for qualified evaluation rather than repeatedly processing questionable loads.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the SYSTEM 1E cycle would not start and repeatedly returned to a not-ready condition.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the processing load positioned so that the door could not achieve proper closure.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the load position, verified proper door closure, and completed a full functional cycle without alarms before returning the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact phase where the cycle stopped
Whether failure repeats unloaded or with another approved setup

title: STERIS SYSTEM 1E Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Door Will Not Lock, Unlock, or Seal
description: Troubleshoots door closure, locking, release, and sealing problems caused by obstruction, load placement, contamination, alignment, utilities, or interlock conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Staff and the Processing Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not force open a locked door or defeat an interlock. If a cycle has been interrupted, treat the load as incompletely processed until handled according to approved procedure. Expected outcome: Personnel remain protected and questionable processed items are isolated. Troubleshooting proceeds only when the unit is safe.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Door Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the door will not close, closes but will not lock, will not remain sealed, will not unlock after a cycle, or intermittently reports an open condition. Record any displayed message. Expected outcome: The specific mechanical or recognition problem is clearly identified. If the condition no longer occurs, cycle the door several times and complete functional verification before stopping.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Obstruction
steps.instructions: Examine accessible door edges, sealing surfaces, latch area, chamber opening, tray, tubing, accessories, and load position. Remove only normal removable debris or incorrectly positioned items within approved external maintenance scope. Expected outcome: Nothing prevents full door movement or seal contact. If removing an obstruction restores normal locking and sealing, verify repeated operation and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Door and Seal Surfaces
steps.instructions: Check for visible damage, contamination, deformation, cuts, loose material, or residue on the accessible sealing surfaces. Do not lubricate, adjust, or replace sealing components unless specifically authorized and trained. Expected outcome: Accessible sealing surfaces appear intact and clean. Visible damage requires removal from service and qualified evaluation.

steps.title: 5. Verify Load Position and Accessory Routing
steps.instructions: Confirm the processing tray, instruments, adapters, tubing, and other accessories remain fully inside their intended area and do not cross the sealing path. Expected outcome: The load does not interfere with door closure. If repositioning the load restores normal operation, perform a full functional cycle before stopping.

steps.title: 6. Verify Power and Cycle State
steps.instructions: Confirm the unit has stable power and determine whether the control system indicates that a cycle is active, aborted, draining, or otherwise not ready for door release. Do not attempt to mechanically override a lock. Expected outcome: The system is in a legitimate state for the requested door action. If normal completion or approved recovery allows the door to release, verify subsequent operation.

steps.title: 7. Check for Utility or Process Conditions Preventing Release
steps.instructions: If the door remains locked after an abnormal cycle, verify whether the system is still managing water, pressure, temperature, draining, or another process condition. Do not force entry into a chamber that may not be in a safe state. Expected outcome: The unit reaches a safe condition and releases the door normally. If it does not, stop external troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Test Door Recognition Without Forcing the Mechanism
steps.instructions: When safe, open and close the door normally and observe whether its status changes correctly on the user interface. Do not adjust switches, sensors, hinges, or internal latching mechanisms without authorized procedures. Expected outcome: Door status tracks actual position consistently. If recognition remains intermittent or incorrect, remove the unit from service.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm repeated normal opening, closing, locking, sealing, and unlocking. Complete an approved functional cycle and inspect for leakage around the door. Expected outcome: The door functions consistently and no leakage or interlock fault occurs. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Door or Interlock Problems
steps.instructions: If obstruction, contamination, load placement, and process state are ruled out but the door still fails to lock, unlock, or seal, discontinue use. Expected outcome: The SYSTEM 1E is routed for qualified service rather than operated with an unreliable safety interlock.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the SYSTEM 1E door would not lock when a processing cycle was selected.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found external tubing from the load routed across the door sealing area.
CCR.Resolution: Repositioned the tubing correctly, confirmed repeated door locking and sealing, and completed a functional cycle without leakage or alarms.

helpfulDetails: Whether the door would not close, lock, unlock, or seal
Cycle state when the issue occurred

title: STERIS SYSTEM 1E Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Chamber Will Not Fill, Drain, or Reach Level
description: Troubleshoots filling, draining, and level problems caused by water supply, drain restrictions, hoses, loading, obstructions, or external utility conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Load and Surrounding Area
steps.instructions: Stop processing if the chamber does not fill or drain correctly. Do not release an incompletely processed load. If water is escaping the unit or accumulating on the floor, isolate the area and remove the system from use. Expected outcome: The load remains controlled and no staff are exposed to an unsafe wet area. Troubleshooting proceeds only when safe.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Fluid Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the chamber does not fill at all, fills slowly, overfills, fails to reach the expected level, drains slowly, or retains water after the cycle. Record the cycle phase and displayed messages. Expected outcome: The fluid-handling failure is clearly characterized. If the condition was temporary, perform a controlled verification cycle before stopping.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility Water Availability
steps.instructions: Confirm the facility water supply serving the unit is available. Check accessible supply valves for proper position and inspect visible supply hoses for kinks, compression, or obvious leakage. Expected outcome: Water reaches the reprocessor without an obvious external restriction. If reopening a supply or correcting a kink restores filling, verify a full cycle and stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Drain Path
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible drain tubing and the nearby facility drain for visible blockage, kinks, backup, or standing water. Determine whether other equipment on the same drain is also affected. Expected outcome: The external drain path is open and flowing normally. If clearing an external facility obstruction restores proper drainage, verify cycle operation and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Chamber and Load for Obstruction
steps.instructions: When safe and accessible, inspect the chamber, tray, visible screens, drain area, tubing, and load position for debris or items blocking normal fluid movement. Perform only cleaning or removal permitted for routine external maintenance. Expected outcome: No visible obstruction interferes with filling or draining. If removing permitted debris corrects the issue, complete functional verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Load Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm accessories, connectors, tubing, and the load are positioned correctly and are not covering fluid openings, pinching hoses, or interfering with level sensing areas. Expected outcome: Load placement does not obstruct normal fluid circulation. If repositioning corrects the problem, verify a full processing cycle and stop.

steps.title: 7. Check for Facility Drain or Water Pressure Changes
steps.instructions: Ask whether building maintenance, water shutdowns, plumbing work, or other utility events occurred. Compare with another nearby fixture or approved device where appropriate. Expected outcome: Facility infrastructure is stable. A confirmed building utility problem should be corrected before further equipment troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Observe a Controlled Fill and Drain Sequence
steps.instructions: If safe, run an approved test cycle and observe filling and draining. Note abnormal delays, repeated cycling, unexpected level behavior, or failure to progress. Expected outcome: The chamber fills and drains normally without leakage or unexplained delay. If successful after an external correction, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm normal water entry, expected progression through fluid phases, complete drainage, cycle completion, and absence of leakage. Inspect the surrounding floor before return to service. Expected outcome: Fluid handling is reliable and the system completes processing normally. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Fluid-Handling Failure
steps.instructions: If supply water, external hoses, load placement, visible obstructions, and facility drainage are acceptable but the condition remains, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The system is removed from service for qualified evaluation of internal fluid-control components.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the SYSTEM 1E would fill slowly and then abort before completing the cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external water supply hose partially kinked behind the unit.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the hose routing, verified normal filling and drainage through a complete functional cycle, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether failure involved fill, drain, or level
Cycle phase where the problem occurred

title: STERIS SYSTEM 1E Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Temperature or Pressure Will Not Reach Setpoint
description: Troubleshoots process temperature or pressure conditions that prevent cycle progression because of utilities, loading, leakage, environmental, or service-level causes.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Load and Stop Questionable Processing
steps.instructions: Do not consider a load successfully processed when the reprocessor cannot achieve or maintain required process conditions. Move processing to another validated workflow. Expected outcome: No potentially underprocessed device is released for clinical use, and troubleshooting occurs without compromising patient care.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether temperature or pressure rises slowly, never reaches the required process value, reaches it and then falls, or produces an abort. Record any displayed message and the point in the cycle where the problem occurs. Expected outcome: The failure pattern is clearly documented. If normal conditions are later achieved, a full verification cycle is still required before return to service.

steps.title: 3. Check for Visible Leakage or Door-Sealing Problems
steps.instructions: Inspect the door area, chamber exterior, hoses, fittings, and surrounding floor for visible leakage. Verify the door closes and seals normally without obstruction. Expected outcome: No external leak or door problem explains the inability to maintain process conditions. If correcting a loading or sealing obstruction restores normal operation, verify a full cycle and stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify Required Facility Utilities
steps.instructions: Confirm required water, electrical power, and any other facility service supporting the process is available and stable. Ask whether utility maintenance or outages recently occurred. Expected outcome: External utilities are available. If restoration of a facility utility corrects the condition, verify complete cycle performance before stopping.

steps.title: 5. Verify Load and Accessory Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that the load, processing tray, tubing, adapters, and accessories are correctly positioned. An incorrectly configured load can interfere with normal circulation or process sensing. Expected outcome: The processing setup is correct. If correcting load configuration restores normal conditions, complete final verification.

steps.title: 6. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Look for obvious environmental factors such as unusually cold incoming water conditions, excessive room temperature, blocked external ventilation, or recent relocation that could affect operation. Do not obstruct ventilation openings. Expected outcome: The equipment is operating in a normal environment without obvious external thermal restrictions.

steps.title: 7. Observe the Process Trend
steps.instructions: Run an approved test cycle while observing displayed temperature, pressure, cycle progression, and alarms. Do not compare values against invented limits; use the system's own normal cycle behavior and approved documentation. Expected outcome: Temperature and pressure progress normally and remain sufficient for cycle completion. If they do after correcting an external cause, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 8. Compare Repeated Behavior
steps.instructions: If permitted, repeat the test with an approved standard load or setup to determine whether the condition follows a particular load arrangement or occurs regardless of load. Expected outcome: A load-related cause is either identified or ruled out. Persistent failure independent of load indicates the need for service escalation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction, complete a full approved cycle and verify normal process progression, absence of leaks or alarms, successful completion indication, and proper cycle record. Expected outcome: The unit reliably reaches and maintains required process conditions. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Process-Control Problem
steps.instructions: If utilities, door sealing, load configuration, and environmental conditions are acceptable but the unit still cannot achieve or maintain its process conditions, discontinue use. Expected outcome: The SYSTEM 1E is removed from service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the SYSTEM 1E repeatedly aborted because the process conditions would not stabilize.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the door sealing area obstructed by an incorrectly positioned processing accessory.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected accessory placement, verified proper door sealing, and completed a full functional cycle with normal process progression and no alarms.

helpfulDetails: Whether temperature, pressure, or both were affected

title: STERIS SYSTEM 1E Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Detergent, Chemistry, or Steam Delivery Fails
description: Troubleshoots missing or inadequate process chemistry or utility delivery caused by consumable installation, supply depletion, connections, loading, or external service conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Load and Do Not Release an Incomplete Process
steps.instructions: If required chemistry or another process medium was not delivered correctly, consider the cycle unsuccessful unless approved procedures specifically establish otherwise. Segregate the affected load. Expected outcome: Patient-ready devices are not released from a questionable process, and alternate validated reprocessing remains available.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Delivery Function Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the reported problem involves detergent, process chemistry, steam or another facility-supplied process service, and whether delivery is completely absent, intermittent, or rejected before the cycle begins. Record displayed messages. Expected outcome: The affected delivery path and cycle phase are identified. If the problem no longer occurs, complete a verification cycle before stopping.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Consumable Is Present
steps.instructions: Check that required chemistry or detergent is available, correctly installed, and appropriate for the system and selected process. Inspect packaging and accessible connections for obvious damage or leakage. Expected outcome: The required consumable is present and properly installed. If installation correction restores normal recognition and delivery, verify a complete cycle and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check Expiration and Condition
steps.instructions: Verify consumables are within their permitted use period and have been stored and handled appropriately according to facility and manufacturer requirements. Do not use damaged, leaking, contaminated, or questionable chemistry. Expected outcome: Consumables are suitable for use. If replacing an unsuitable consumable resolves the problem, perform functional verification and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Tubing and Connections
steps.instructions: Check external tubing, connectors, pickup points, and fittings associated with delivery for disconnection, kinking, pinching, blockage, or leakage. Do not open internal chemical-delivery assemblies. Expected outcome: External delivery paths are correctly connected and unobstructed. If correcting a connection restores delivery, verify through a complete cycle.

steps.title: 6. Verify Facility-Supplied Utilities
steps.instructions: For any delivery function dependent on building utilities, confirm the required service is available and accessible valves are open. Determine whether maintenance or utility outages recently occurred. Expected outcome: Facility service is present. If restoration of the utility corrects the problem, complete a verification cycle and stop.

steps.title: 7. Verify Load and Cycle Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm the selected process and load configuration require the consumables and accessories currently installed. Avoid changing protected process configuration merely to bypass an alarm. Expected outcome: The correct approved process setup is being used. If setup correction resolves the issue, verify cycle completion.

steps.title: 8. Observe an Approved Test Cycle
steps.instructions: Run a controlled test cycle when safe and observe whether the system recognizes and uses the required consumable or utility without alarms. Do not expose personnel to process chemicals while inspecting operation. Expected outcome: Required delivery occurs normally and the cycle progresses to completion. If successful, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify consumable recognition, process progression, absence of leaks, successful cycle completion, and accurate cycle documentation. Expected outcome: Delivery is reliable and the SYSTEM 1E completes its process normally. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Delivery Failure
steps.instructions: If correct consumables, external tubing, facility utilities, and process selection are verified but delivery still fails, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The system is removed from service for evaluation of internal delivery or control components.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the SYSTEM 1E would not proceed because the required process chemistry was not being recognized.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the consumable connection was not fully seated.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the approved consumable connection, verified normal recognition and delivery during a complete functional cycle, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Which consumable or delivery function failed

title: STERIS SYSTEM 1E Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Leak Test or Process Challenge Test Fails
description: Troubleshoots failed leak or process challenge testing caused by setup, connections, accessories, load condition, consumables, or unresolved equipment performance problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Device and Do Not Continue Processing
steps.instructions: A failed leak or process challenge test can indicate that the endoscope, accessory, processing setup, or reprocessor is not suitable for continued use. Do not advance the affected load as though the test passed. Expected outcome: The affected device or load remains segregated until the cause is identified. Alternate validated processing is used as necessary.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Test Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the failure involved an endoscope leak test, an equipment process check, or another required challenge test. Record the exact displayed message, test phase, and affected device or load. Expected outcome: The specific failure is documented. If the test passes on a repeat attempt, the original setup must still be evaluated before the unit is considered reliable.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Endoscope or Test Article Externally
steps.instructions: If an endoscope-specific test failed, inspect the scope, connectors, valves, channels, caps, and accessible surfaces for obvious damage or incorrect setup. Do not continue processing a device with visible damage. Expected outcome: No obvious device defect or setup problem is present. Visible damage requires the affected endoscope to be removed from clinical use and handled under its service procedure.

steps.title: 4. Verify Test Connections
steps.instructions: Confirm leak-test connectors, adapters, tubing, channel connections, and processing accessories are fully seated and appropriate for the device being processed. Check for kinks, loose fittings, or missing required components. Expected outcome: All external test connections are correct. If reseating a connection allows a successful test, repeat verification and stop once reliability is demonstrated.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessories for Damage or Moisture
steps.instructions: Check reusable or approved accessories for cracks, damaged seals, contamination, retained moisture, or other visible conditions that could affect testing. Expected outcome: Accessories appear serviceable. If a damaged accessory is replaced with an approved known-good equivalent and the test passes, complete final verification.

steps.title: 6. Use an Approved Known-Good Comparison
steps.instructions: When permitted, test with a known-good compatible accessory or processing setup to determine whether the failure follows the original device/accessory or remains with the SYSTEM 1E. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to either the load/accessory or the reprocessor. If a known-good setup passes consistently, address the affected accessory or device separately.

steps.title: 7. Verify Consumables and Utilities
steps.instructions: Confirm required chemistry, water, power, and other process supplies are normal. A process challenge may fail because the underlying cycle conditions are not being achieved. Expected outcome: External process conditions are available and acceptable.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Test Only After Correcting a Plausible Cause
steps.instructions: Do not repeatedly rerun a failed test without intervention. After correcting a connection, accessory, setup, or external condition, repeat the approved test. Expected outcome: The test passes consistently after a clearly identified correction. If so, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify the test passes using an approved setup and that the associated processing cycle completes without alarms. Confirm test and cycle records are generated as expected. Expected outcome: The test and subsequent cycle perform reliably. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Repeated Test Failure
steps.instructions: If setup, device condition, connectors, accessories, consumables, and utilities have been verified but testing still fails, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The affected equipment is removed from service and evaluated by qualified personnel.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported repeated leak-test failures when connecting an endoscope to the SYSTEM 1E.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external leak-test connection was not fully seated.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the connection, repeated the approved test successfully, and verified completion of a functional processing cycle before returning the reprocessor to service.

title: STERIS SYSTEM 1E Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Load Remains Wet or Cleaning Results Are Poor
description: Troubleshoots unexpectedly wet loads or poor processing results associated with loading, drainage, channel connections, consumables, utilities, or incomplete cycles.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Safety and Quarantine Questionable Items
steps.instructions: Do not release a device if processing results are questionable. A visibly soiled device, an incompletely processed device, or a load associated with an abnormal cycle must be reprocessed according to approved policy. Expected outcome: Questionable instruments remain out of clinical use while processing performance is investigated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Result
steps.instructions: Determine whether the concern is retained water, visible soil, residue, inconsistent results, specific channels not being processed, or a general perception that the load is wetter than expected. Confirm whether the cycle completed normally. Expected outcome: The complaint is defined accurately. If the issue is unrelated to an actual process failure, document the observation and verify normal equipment performance.

steps.title: 3. Confirm Pre-Cleaning Requirements Were Completed
steps.instructions: Verify the endoscope or device received the required bedside and manual pre-cleaning steps before automated processing. Clinical Engineering should not attribute poor results to the reprocessor until upstream workflow is considered. Expected outcome: Required pre-cleaning was completed. If poor results are caused by missed upstream cleaning steps, correct the workflow and verify subsequent processing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Load Arrangement
steps.instructions: Check that the device, tubing, adapters, and accessories were arranged correctly and that loops, folds, or positioning do not trap fluid or restrict circulation. Expected outcome: Load orientation supports normal fluid flow and drainage. If repositioning corrects the result, verify another approved cycle and stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify Channel and Accessory Connections
steps.instructions: Confirm all required connections are complete, secure, and appropriate for the endoscope or accessory. Check for disconnected, kinked, or visibly damaged tubing. Expected outcome: All required channels and accessories are connected correctly. If correction restores acceptable results, verify cycle performance and stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify Consumables
steps.instructions: Confirm the approved chemistry or detergent is present, properly installed, and suitable for use. Do not substitute materials or alter process concentrations outside approved procedures. Expected outcome: Required consumables are available and correctly configured. If replacing or reseating a consumable corrects the issue, complete functional verification.

steps.title: 7. Check Fill and Drain Performance
steps.instructions: Observe whether the chamber fills and drains normally and whether water remains unexpectedly after cycle completion. Inspect accessible drains and external hoses for restriction. Expected outcome: Fluid movement and final drainage are normal. If correcting an external drain restriction resolves retained moisture, verify a full cycle and stop.

steps.title: 8. Review Cycle Completion and Alarms
steps.instructions: Confirm that the affected load actually completed the intended cycle without abort, alarm, or interruption. A load from an incomplete cycle should not be evaluated as a normal processing result. Expected outcome: Only fully completed cycles are used to judge equipment performance.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Run an approved test load or known-good setup and verify proper circulation, drainage, cycle completion, and acceptable post-process condition according to facility and manufacturer requirements. Expected outcome: Processing results are repeatable and acceptable. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Poor Processing Results
steps.instructions: If pre-cleaning, loading, connections, consumables, and drainage are correct but poor results continue, remove the reprocessor from use. Expected outcome: The SYSTEM 1E is evaluated for an internal circulation, delivery, sensing, or process-control problem.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported endoscopes were retaining excessive water after completed SYSTEM 1E cycles.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external drain hose partially restricted by its routing behind the unit.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the drain hose routing, completed a functional cycle with normal drainage, and verified acceptable post-cycle condition before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the concern was moisture, visible soil, or residue

title: STERIS SYSTEM 1E Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Printer, Cycle Record, or Tracking Interface Fails
description: Troubleshoots missing printouts, cycle records, or tracking communication caused by media, connections, peripherals, network paths, configuration, or external systems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Traceability Before Continuing Routine Use
steps.instructions: Determine whether the failure affects required documentation, load traceability, or release of processed devices. Follow facility policy for manual documentation or alternate processing if required records cannot be reliably produced. Expected outcome: Processing records remain traceable and no load is released contrary to facility documentation requirements.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Function Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the printer does not print, a cycle record is missing or incomplete, data cannot be saved, or an external tracking interface does not receive the record. Confirm whether processing itself completes normally. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to printing, local recording, or external communication.

steps.title: 3. Check the Printer and Media
steps.instructions: If a printer is used, confirm power, paper or approved media, cover closure, accessible connections, and absence of obvious jams. Replace only approved consumables according to normal procedures. Expected outcome: The printer is ready and properly supplied. If correcting media or a simple jam restores printing, test another record and stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify External Cables and Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible data, printer, network, or interface cables for looseness, damage, incorrect routing, or accidental disconnection. Expected outcome: External communication connections are secure and intact. If reseating a cable restores normal operation, verify another complete record transfer and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Equipment Status and Date/Time Display
steps.instructions: Confirm the system is otherwise operating normally and that visible identification, date, time, cycle, and operator-related information appear reasonable. Do not make unauthorized configuration changes. Expected outcome: Local system information appears normal. Configuration discrepancies should be documented and escalated if protected settings require service access.

steps.title: 6. Determine Whether the Failure Is Local or External
steps.instructions: Check whether the record exists locally but fails to print or transmit. If an external tracking system is involved, determine whether other connected devices are also affected. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the SYSTEM 1E, printer, network path, or tracking infrastructure. A broader outage should be routed to the responsible IT or integration team.

steps.title: 7. Verify Network or Interface Availability
steps.instructions: For networked tracking, inspect accessible network link indicators and connections. Confirm that the intended interface path is available without altering VLAN, IP, server, or protected configuration unless specifically authorized. Expected outcome: The external communication path is available. If infrastructure restoration resolves the issue, verify successful data transfer and stop.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Record Test
steps.instructions: Run an approved test or use an appropriate completed cycle record to verify printing or transmission. Confirm the correct record reaches the expected destination. Expected outcome: Documentation is produced accurately and consistently. If so, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm cycle completion, record generation, printer operation if applicable, and successful transmission or tracking entry. Verify traceability before returning the unit to unrestricted use. Expected outcome: Required documentation functions are restored and reliable. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Documentation Failure
steps.instructions: If media, peripherals, cables, network availability, and external systems are ruled out but records still fail, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The affected function is routed for qualified equipment, IT, or integration service.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported completed SYSTEM 1E cycles were not producing printed cycle records.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external printer connection loose at the reprocessor.
CCR.Resolution: Secured the printer connection, verified successful printing of a subsequent cycle record, and confirmed normal cycle documentation before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the failure involved printing, local storage, or tracking

title: STERIS SYSTEM 1E Endoscope Reprocessor (AER) - Overtemperature, Leak, or Water-on-Floor Condition Occurs
description: Troubleshoots overheating, visible leakage, or water around the SYSTEM 1E while prioritizing electrical safety, containment, external plumbing, loading, and escalation.

steps.title: 1. Stop Use and Protect Staff Immediately
steps.instructions: If water is actively leaking, the floor is wet, the unit is unusually hot, or an overtemperature condition is reported, stop the cycle when safe and remove the equipment from clinical use. Keep personnel away from wet electrical areas. Expected outcome: Exposure to electrical, slip, thermal, and chemical hazards is minimized. Active unsafe conditions are contained before troubleshooting continues.

steps.title: 2. Preserve the Load as Potentially Incompletely Processed
steps.instructions: Do not release a load from an interrupted or abnormal cycle. Follow facility procedure for handling and reprocessing affected devices. Expected outcome: No questionable load enters patient use.

steps.title: 3. Determine the Source and Timing
steps.instructions: Ask whether the leak occurred during filling, processing, draining, or while idle. Determine whether water came from the door area, an external hose, a facility connection, a drain backup, or an unknown location. Record any overtemperature or leak message. Expected outcome: The event is characterized without unnecessary operation of the equipment.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Area Before Re-Energizing
steps.instructions: With the equipment in a safe state, inspect the power cord, floor, external hoses, fittings, drain connection, door area, and nearby plumbing. Do not energize equipment standing in water or showing signs of electrical contamination. Expected outcome: No immediate electrical hazard is present. If water has contacted electrical components or the source cannot be safely isolated, leave the unit out of service.

steps.title: 5. Check External Water Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible water supply hoses, fittings, valves, and connections for looseness, cracks, damage, or obvious leakage. Expected outcome: External supply connections are dry and secure. If an authorized external connection correction eliminates the leak, continue with controlled verification.

steps.title: 6. Check the Drain Path
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible drain hoses and the facility drain for kinks, blockage, backup, or overflow. Determine whether another nearby fixture indicates a facility drainage problem. Expected outcome: Drainage is unobstructed. If a facility drain problem caused the water-on-floor event, correct the infrastructure issue before testing the reprocessor.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Door, Seal, and Load Position
steps.instructions: Check for debris, accessories, tubing, or load components interfering with door closure or sealing. Do not adjust or dismantle the door or seal mechanism without approved service procedures. Expected outcome: The door closes without obstruction and no visible damage is present. If correcting load placement resolves leakage, proceed with cautious verification.

steps.title: 8. Assess Ventilation and Heat Conditions
steps.instructions: For an overtemperature complaint, inspect accessible ventilation openings for blockage and confirm the surrounding environment is not unusually hot. Look for abnormal fan noise, odor, discoloration, or excessive external heat. Expected outcome: Ventilation is unobstructed and there are no signs of continuing overheating. Persistent overheating requires removal from service.

steps.title: 9. Perform Controlled Functional Verification Only if Safe
steps.instructions: If the source was an external, clearly corrected condition and there is no electrical or chemical hazard, perform an approved test cycle while observing for leaks, abnormal temperature, drainage problems, and alarms. Expected outcome: The cycle completes with no leakage, overheating, abnormal odor, or water accumulation. Troubleshooting can stop after required return-to-service checks.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Any Unexplained or Recurrent Leak or Overtemperature Condition
steps.instructions: Do not continue operating a SYSTEM 1E that repeatedly leaks, overheats, or places water near electrical components. Expected outcome: The equipment remains removed from service until qualified evaluation and corrective action are completed.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported water collecting behind the SYSTEM 1E during the drain portion of a cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external drain hose partially displaced and leaking at its accessible connection.
CCR.Resolution: Secured the drain connection, dried and inspected the area, completed a monitored functional cycle with no further leakage, and verified normal operation before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the event involved overheating, leakage, or both
Drain hose and facility drain condition
Presence of odor, heat, or electrical damage

title: STERIS Reliance Vision Cart Washer - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Addresses loss of power, incomplete startup, blank controls, or startup interruptions caused by power, disconnects, interlocks, controls, or facility conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patients, Staff, and Processing Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a cart washer that cannot complete startup. Redirect carts, containers, or other approved loads to another verified processing method according to facility procedure. If there is smoke, unusual odor, visible electrical damage, water near electrical components, or repeated breaker operation, remove the washer from service immediately. Expected outcome: Processing continues through an alternate verified method while the affected washer is evaluated safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Complaint
steps.instructions: Ask staff what occurred when the unit was last operated. Determine whether the washer is completely dead, displays briefly and shuts down, stops during initialization, or remains at a startup screen. Observe available displays and indicators without bypassing any safety devices. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to loss of incoming power, control startup, or a startup condition preventing readiness.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility Power and External Disconnects
steps.instructions: Confirm that the washer's normal facility power source and any accessible designated disconnects are in their expected operating positions. Check for evidence of a local or area power interruption. Do not repeatedly reset a breaker or disconnect that trips again. Expected outcome: Stable facility power is available to the washer. If restoring an approved external power source allows normal startup, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Power-Related Conditions
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible power cords, conduit interfaces, disconnect enclosures, and surrounding areas for looseness, damage, heat discoloration, moisture, or signs of impact. Do not open energized electrical compartments unless specifically authorized and trained to do so under facility and manufacturer procedures. Expected outcome: No obvious external power defect or unsafe condition is present.

steps.title: 5. Verify Doors and External Safety Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm that all loading and unloading doors are fully closed and unobstructed. Check for carts, racks, debris, or damaged seals preventing the unit from recognizing a safe startup condition. Verify that accessible emergency-stop or similar safety controls are not activated. Expected outcome: External safety conditions permit normal startup. If the unit starts normally after correcting a door or control condition, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Check Utilities Required for Initialization
steps.instructions: Verify that required facility utilities serving the washer are available and that accessible supply valves are in their normal operating positions. Look for facility utility outages or maintenance affecting the area. Do not alter regulated facility utility settings. Expected outcome: Required utilities are available and stable enough for the washer to initialize.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: If no unsafe condition exists, perform a normal shutdown and restart using approved operating controls. Allow the complete startup sequence to finish without interrupting it. Record any displayed message or point at which startup stops. Expected outcome: The washer reaches its normal ready state. If it does, proceed to a functional cycle verification and stop troubleshooting if successful.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Run an approved empty or test cycle appropriate for the department and confirm normal startup, controls, door behavior, utility response, alarms, and cycle initiation. Do not return the washer to service based only on the display powering on. Expected outcome: The washer starts normally and completes the required functional verification without abnormal indications.

steps.title: 9. Escalate if Startup Still Fails
steps.instructions: If facility power, external controls, doors, utilities, and normal restart conditions are satisfactory but startup still fails, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The unit is removed from service for qualified service evaluation rather than subjected to unnecessary internal troubleshooting.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance Vision cart washer would not complete startup and remained unavailable for cycles.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the washer had facility power but an accessible emergency-stop control remained engaged.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering restored the control to its normal position, restarted the washer, and verified normal startup and successful functional cycle operation.

helpfulDetails: Whether the unit was completely dead or partially powered
Evidence of water, heat, odor, or damage

title: STERIS Reliance Vision Cart Washer - Cycle Will Not Start, Aborts, or Stalls
description: Addresses cycles that cannot begin, stop unexpectedly, or remain in one phase because of doors, utilities, loading, settings, or external conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a washer that cannot consistently complete its programmed cycle. Remove the affected load from the normal workflow and process it using another approved method. Do not repeatedly restart a partially completed cleaning cycle and assume the load is acceptable. Expected outcome: Questionable loads are withheld from use and processing continues through an alternate verified method.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Where the Cycle Fails
steps.instructions: Determine whether the cycle refuses to start, aborts immediately, stops at a repeatable phase, or appears stalled without advancing. Record the selected cycle and any displayed message or alarm before clearing it. Expected outcome: The failure is associated with a specific stage or prerequisite rather than described only as a general cycle failure.

steps.title: 3. Verify Door Closure and Interlocks Externally
steps.instructions: Inspect both sides of the washer as applicable. Confirm doors are fully closed, free of obstruction, and not being held out of position by racks, carts, debris, or damaged sealing surfaces. Do not bypass a door interlock. Expected outcome: Doors are properly positioned and recognized. If the cycle starts normally afterward, continue through completion and stop troubleshooting if successful.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Load and Rack Position
steps.instructions: Confirm the load is correctly positioned and does not interfere with doors, spray components, sensors, or movement of the rack or cart. Check that removable racks or accessories are seated normally and are appropriate for the selected process. Expected outcome: The load does not physically interfere with cycle initiation or progression.

steps.title: 5. Verify Cycle Selection and Controls
steps.instructions: Confirm that an appropriate cycle has been selected and that the operator controls respond normally. Check for unintended pause, hold, or incomplete selections visible from the normal interface. Do not enter restricted service menus or alter validated process parameters. Expected outcome: A valid cycle is selected and normal controls allow initiation.

steps.title: 6. Verify Facility Utilities
steps.instructions: Confirm that water, steam, drainage, electrical supply, and other required external utilities are available to the washer as applicable. Check whether other nearby equipment is experiencing the same utility problem. Expected outcome: External utilities are available and stable. If restoring a facility utility allows the cycle to complete normally, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Accessible Chemistry Supplies
steps.instructions: Check detergent or other required chemistry containers, pickup tubing, visible connections, and supply status for depletion, disconnection, kinks, or obvious leaks. Use only approved chemistry and handling procedures. Expected outcome: Required chemistry is available and externally connected correctly.

steps.title: 8. Attempt a Controlled Test Cycle
steps.instructions: Once external causes have been corrected, run an approved empty or test load cycle and observe whether the machine advances normally through its phases. Do not leave a repeatedly stalling washer in clinical use. Expected outcome: The test cycle starts, progresses normally, and completes without aborting or stalling. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Repeatable Cycle Failure
steps.instructions: If the washer repeatedly stops at the same phase despite correct loading, doors, utilities, chemistry, and cycle selection, remove it from service. Expected outcome: A repeatable service-level problem is escalated without unauthorized internal repair.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance Vision cart washer started normally but repeatedly stopped before completing the selected cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the loading rack was positioned incorrectly and prevented the door from fully reaching its normal closed position.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering repositioned the rack, verified correct door closure, and confirmed the washer completed a full test cycle normally.

helpfulDetails: Results of an empty or test cycle

title: STERIS Reliance Vision Cart Washer - Door Will Not Lock, Unlock, or Seal
description: Addresses door movement, locking, unlocking, or sealing problems caused by obstruction, load position, contamination, alignment, controls, or cycle state.

steps.title: 1. Protect Staff and Processing Continuity
steps.instructions: Do not operate the washer with a door that cannot reliably close, lock, unlock, or seal. Prevent staff from forcing the door or bypassing interlocks. Redirect processing to another verified washer if needed. Expected outcome: Personnel are protected from unexpected door movement, hot water, steam, and incomplete containment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Door Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the affected door will not close, will not latch or lock, remains locked after the cycle, leaks at the seal, or gives an indication that the door is not secure. Record whether the issue affects the loading side, unloading side, or both. Expected outcome: The specific door function and affected side are identified.

steps.title: 3. Check for Physical Obstruction
steps.instructions: Inspect the doorway and threshold for carts, racks, utensils, packaging, debris, labels, or other material preventing full travel. Remove only accessible debris that can be cleared safely without disassembly. Expected outcome: The door path is unobstructed. If normal operation returns, perform a functional verification and stop troubleshooting if successful.

steps.title: 4. Verify Load and Rack Position
steps.instructions: Confirm that the cart or rack is fully positioned within the chamber and is not contacting the door or seal. Look for shifted loads or protruding items. Expected outcome: The load remains clear of the door's full range of travel.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Sealing Surfaces
steps.instructions: Visually inspect the door seal and mating surfaces for debris, folded material, visible damage, contamination, or anything preventing uniform contact. Do not stretch, remove, or modify seals unless specifically authorized by service documentation. Expected outcome: Sealing surfaces are clean, intact, and unobstructed.

steps.title: 6. Verify Cycle State and Normal Controls
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine is in a state in which the door is expected to move or unlock. A door may remain secured while a cycle condition is active or until the machine reaches a safe release condition. Use only normal operator controls. Expected outcome: Door behavior corresponds with the washer's cycle state, or the abnormal condition is confirmed.

steps.title: 7. Check for Utility or Power Interruption
steps.instructions: If the door stopped functioning after a power or utility interruption, verify normal facility power and allow the washer to return to its normal ready state using approved procedures. Do not force a locked door after a power interruption. Expected outcome: Normal power and control conditions are restored. If the door subsequently operates correctly, proceed to functional verification.

steps.title: 8. Test Door Operation Without a Clinical Load
steps.instructions: When safe and permitted, operate the door through a normal open-close sequence and then initiate an approved test cycle to confirm locking and sealing. Observe for abnormal noise, binding, hesitation, or leakage. Expected outcome: The door closes, locks, seals, and releases normally. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Remove from Service for Persistent Door Failure
steps.instructions: If the door binds, fails to lock, remains locked unexpectedly, or leaks despite correct loading and clean sealing surfaces, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The washer is withheld from use until qualified service evaluates the door system.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance Vision loading door would not close and the washer would not start a cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loading rack was not fully seated and was interfering with door travel.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering repositioned the rack, verified normal door closure and locking, and completed a successful test cycle.

helpfulDetails: Whether the door failed to close, lock, unlock, or seal
Cycle state when the issue occurred
Results of final door and cycle test

title: STERIS Reliance Vision Cart Washer - Chamber Will Not Fill, Drain, or Reach Level
description: Addresses improper chamber filling, draining, or water level caused by utility supply, drainage, obstruction, loading, or service-level flow-control problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Staff and Processing Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not continue cycling the washer if water level is abnormal, drainage is incomplete, or water is backing up. Prevent exposure to hot water and contaminated process water. Redirect loads to another approved washer. Expected outcome: The affected washer is not relied upon while water handling is uncertain.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Whether the Problem Is Fill, Level, or Drain Related
steps.instructions: Determine whether the chamber receives no water, fills slowly, appears to overfill, fails to reach the required cycle condition, or retains water after a phase or completed cycle. Record the exact phase and any displayed message. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to incoming water, level control, or drainage.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility Water Availability
steps.instructions: Confirm the required facility water supplies are available and that accessible supply valves serving the washer are in their normal positions. Check whether nearby processing equipment is experiencing the same supply issue. Expected outcome: Facility water is available at the washer. If restoring an external supply corrects the issue, complete a test cycle and stop troubleshooting if successful.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Supply Connections
steps.instructions: Check visible hoses, pipes, strainers or external connection points that can be inspected without disassembly for kinks, leakage, damage, or evidence of restricted flow. Do not alter plumbing controls outside Clinical Engineering responsibility. Expected outcome: No accessible supply restriction or leak is found.

steps.title: 5. Check the Chamber and Drain Area for Accessible Obstruction
steps.instructions: When the washer is safe and cool, inspect accessible chamber surfaces, drain screens, and removable strainers for debris or foreign material that may restrict drainage. Use appropriate PPE and facility decontamination procedures. Expected outcome: Accessible drainage paths are free of obvious obstruction. If cleaning an approved removable screen restores proper drainage, verify with a full test cycle.

steps.title: 6. Verify Rack and Load Position
steps.instructions: Confirm carts, racks, and large items are positioned correctly and are not blocking drains, interfering with water distribution, or obstructing accessible level-related areas. Expected outcome: Loading does not interfere with normal water movement.

steps.title: 7. Check Facility Drainage
steps.instructions: Inspect for slow floor drainage, backed-up plumbing, or evidence that the facility drain cannot accept washer discharge. If an infrastructure drain problem is suspected, involve Facilities rather than disassembling the washer. Expected outcome: Facility drainage accepts discharge normally.

steps.title: 8. Run an Approved Test Cycle
steps.instructions: Observe a test cycle from outside the closed washer. Confirm the unit fills, advances normally, drains between appropriate phases, and finishes without standing water or abnormal leakage. Do not open the chamber during an active hazardous phase. Expected outcome: Water handling returns to normal. If the test cycle completes correctly, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Water-Level Problems
steps.instructions: If supplies and drains are available, accessible screens are clear, and loading is correct but filling or draining remains abnormal, remove the washer from service. Expected outcome: Internal flow-control or sensing issues are referred for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance Vision cart washer retained water in the chamber and would not complete the cycle normally.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found debris obstructing an accessible chamber drain screen.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the debris using approved handling precautions, reinstalled the screen, and verified normal fill, drain, and cycle completion.

title: STERIS Reliance Vision Cart Washer - Temperature or Pressure Will Not Reach Setpoint
description: Addresses cycles that cannot achieve required process temperature or pressure because of utility supply, loading, steam, water, controls, or service-level problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing Integrity
steps.instructions: Do not release a load from a cycle that failed to achieve the required validated process conditions. Quarantine or reprocess the load according to facility policy. Use another verified washer until the affected unit is proven functional. Expected outcome: Loads with uncertain processing conditions are not released for clinical use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves temperature, pressure, or both. Record the selected cycle, affected phase, and any displayed message. Do not assume the displayed value itself is inaccurate without supporting evidence. Expected outcome: The affected process parameter and phase are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Relevant Facility Utilities
steps.instructions: Confirm the facility supplies required for the selected process are available. This may include hot water, cold water, steam, electrical power, or other installed utilities. Check whether other equipment supplied from the same infrastructure is experiencing similar problems. Expected outcome: Required utilities are available. If a facility utility issue is corrected and the washer subsequently performs normally, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Utility Connections
steps.instructions: Check visible supply lines, hoses, valves, and connection points for obvious closure, kinking, leakage, or damage. Do not adjust facility steam pressure, regulators, or other controlled infrastructure settings unless specifically authorized. Expected outcome: External utility paths appear intact and available.

steps.title: 5. Verify Load Size and Position
steps.instructions: Confirm that the washer is not improperly loaded and that the selected cycle is appropriate for the intended load. Overloading or incorrect positioning can interfere with effective process conditions even when the washer itself is operating. Expected outcome: Loading is appropriate and does not obstruct circulation or process performance.

steps.title: 6. Confirm Normal Cycle and Settings
steps.instructions: Verify that the correct cycle is selected and that no unauthorized process configuration changes have been made. Do not alter validated temperature, exposure, or other process parameters to force a cycle to complete. Expected outcome: The washer is using its normal validated configuration.

steps.title: 7. Observe an Approved Test Cycle
steps.instructions: Run an approved empty or test cycle and observe whether the displayed temperature or pressure progresses normally. Document whether the problem consistently occurs at the same phase. Expected outcome: The required process condition is achieved normally. If the test cycle completes successfully, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Independent Verification When Authorized
steps.instructions: If applicable and available within the department's approved testing process, use suitable calibrated test equipment to verify whether the reported process condition is credible. Do not substitute an informal measurement for a required manufacturer test method. Expected outcome: The washer's performance is either verified or a discrepancy is documented for service escalation.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Unresolved Process-Condition Failure
steps.instructions: If facility utilities, loading, cycle selection, and external connections are correct but required temperature or pressure still cannot be achieved, remove the washer from service. Expected outcome: A potentially internal heating, sensing, flow, steam, or control problem is escalated appropriately.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance Vision repeatedly failed to reach the expected process temperature during a wash cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the facility steam supply to the washer had been isolated following nearby maintenance.
CCR.Resolution: Facilities restored the steam supply, and Clinical Engineering verified the washer completed a full test cycle with normal process progression.

title: STERIS Reliance Vision Cart Washer - Detergent, Chemistry, or Steam Delivery Fails
description: Addresses absent or unreliable detergent, chemistry, or steam delivery caused by depleted supplies, tubing, connections, facility utilities, or service-level dosing problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Load and Staff
steps.instructions: Do not release loads from cycles in which required detergent, chemistry, or steam delivery was missing or uncertain. Follow PPE and chemical-handling requirements when inspecting chemical supplies. Expected outcome: Potentially inadequately processed loads are withheld and staff are protected from chemical exposure.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Supply Is Affected
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves detergent, another approved chemistry, steam, or multiple supplies. Record the cycle phase and any visible message, alarm, or absence of expected supply usage. Expected outcome: The affected supply path is identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Chemistry Quantity
steps.instructions: Inspect the correct approved chemistry container and confirm that sufficient product is available. Do not substitute an unapproved chemical or dilute a product to keep the washer operating. Expected outcome: The required chemistry is present in sufficient quantity.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Pickup Tubing and External Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible chemical pickup tubing, container caps, fittings, and external connections for disconnection, kinking, pinching, cracking, or obvious leakage. Confirm the pickup tube is actually positioned in the intended container. Expected outcome: The chemistry supply path is correctly connected and unobstructed externally. If correcting the connection restores delivery, proceed to cycle verification and stop troubleshooting if successful.

steps.title: 5. Verify Correct Chemistry Identification
steps.instructions: Confirm that the connected container is the intended approved product and that supply lines have not been inadvertently switched during container replacement or housekeeping. Do not reconfigure dosing values without approved service documentation. Expected outcome: The correct chemistry is connected to the correct supply path.

steps.title: 6. Verify Steam Utility Availability
steps.instructions: For a steam-related complaint, confirm that the facility steam supply serving the washer is available and that accessible valves are in their normal operating positions. Check whether other steam-fed equipment is affected. Expected outcome: The facility steam source is available. Infrastructure problems are referred to Facilities.

steps.title: 7. Inspect for External Leaks
steps.instructions: Look for detergent, chemical, condensate, or steam-related leakage around accessible supply connections and the surrounding equipment area. If a hazardous chemical leak or uncontrolled steam release is present, remove the unit from service immediately. Expected outcome: No unsafe external leakage is present.

steps.title: 8. Run an Approved Test Cycle
steps.instructions: After correcting any external supply problem, run an approved test cycle and verify that the cycle progresses normally and that required supply delivery is no longer reported as missing. Use only approved methods to confirm dosing or utility performance. Expected outcome: The washer completes the test cycle without supply-related fault or interruption. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Delivery Failure
steps.instructions: If chemistry is available, tubing is connected correctly, steam is present, and the failure persists, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Internal dosing, valve, pump, steam-control, sensing, or control issues are referred for qualified service.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance Vision was not drawing detergent during wash cycles.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the detergent pickup tubing disconnected from the approved chemistry container.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering restored the external tubing connection and verified normal cycle operation and detergent supply usage during a test cycle.

title: STERIS Reliance Vision Cart Washer - Leak Test or Process Challenge Test Fails
description: Addresses failed leak-related or process challenge verification caused by setup, loading, utilities, accessories, test materials, or washer performance problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing Integrity
steps.instructions: Do not return the washer to routine processing based on an unsuccessful required verification or challenge result. Hold affected loads according to facility policy and use another verified processing pathway. Expected outcome: The washer remains unavailable for routine use until the required verification is successfully completed.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Test That Failed
steps.instructions: Identify the specific facility, manufacturer, or quality-system test being performed and document the result exactly as observed. Do not substitute a different test or reinterpret a failed result as acceptable. Expected outcome: The failed verification and its acceptance criteria source are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Test Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm that the test materials, indicators, challenge device, rack, or accessories were prepared and positioned according to the applicable approved procedure. Check for obvious setup errors before assuming machine failure. Expected outcome: The test setup is valid. If an obvious setup error is corrected, repeat only as permitted by the applicable procedure.

steps.title: 4. Check Expiration and Condition of Test Materials
steps.instructions: Verify that any consumable test material is within its usable period and has been stored and handled appropriately. Do not use damaged, contaminated, or questionable challenge materials. Expected outcome: Test materials are suitable for use.

steps.title: 5. Verify Washer Loading and Rack Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that the rack, cart, or challenge load is positioned correctly and does not obstruct spray patterns, drainage, or other required process paths. Expected outcome: The test configuration allows the washer to perform as intended.

steps.title: 6. Verify Utilities and Chemistry
steps.instructions: Confirm required water, steam, drainage, power, and chemistry supplies are available and normal. A marginal infrastructure condition can cause a process test to fail without an obvious mechanical breakdown. Expected outcome: External utilities and supplies are normal.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Accessible Chamber Components
steps.instructions: When safe, inspect accessible spray arms, nozzles, screens, and chamber areas for obvious debris or obstruction. Do not disassemble internal systems beyond routine approved access. Expected outcome: Accessible process-delivery components are free of obvious obstruction.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Verification Using the Approved Procedure
steps.instructions: If an identifiable external or setup cause was corrected, repeat the required test exactly according to the applicable facility or manufacturer procedure. Do not repeatedly test a failing machine without investigating the cause. Expected outcome: The washer passes the required test. If it does, document the result and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 9. Escalate a Repeated Valid Test Failure
steps.instructions: If the test is set up correctly, materials are valid, utilities are normal, and the washer still fails, remove it from service. Expected outcome: A possible internal process-performance issue is referred for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance Vision failed the department's required process challenge verification.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the challenge load had been positioned incorrectly and was obstructing normal spray exposure.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the load position, repeated the approved verification with staff, and confirmed a passing result before returning the washer to service.

title: STERIS Reliance Vision Cart Washer - Load Remains Wet or Cleaning Results Are Poor
description: Addresses wet loads, visible soil, residue, or inconsistent cleaning caused by loading, spray obstruction, chemistry, utilities, drainage, or process-performance problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing Quality
steps.instructions: Do not release a visibly soiled or otherwise unacceptable load for clinical use. Reprocess the load according to facility procedure after the washer problem has been addressed. Use another verified washer if needed. Expected outcome: Inadequately processed items do not enter clinical service.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Quality Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the concern is retained moisture, visible soil, residue, spotting, inconsistent cleaning, or a combination. Ask whether the issue affects every load, certain cart positions, or only specific load types. Expected outcome: The symptom pattern is defined well enough to guide troubleshooting.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Load Arrangement
steps.instructions: Confirm that carts, basins, containers, and other approved items are positioned so that surfaces can be reached by the washer process and can drain. Look for nested items, blocked openings, overturned containers, or items shielding one another. Expected outcome: The load is arranged to permit adequate cleaning and drainage. If repositioning resolves the problem on a repeat cycle, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check for Overloading
steps.instructions: Confirm the rack or cart has not been overloaded beyond normal facility practice or arranged so densely that spray and drainage are restricted. Expected outcome: The load allows normal water and air movement.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Spray Components
steps.instructions: When safe, inspect accessible spray arms and nozzles for obvious debris, blockage, or inability to move as intended. Remove only debris that can be cleared through normal approved user-accessible maintenance. Expected outcome: Accessible spray paths are unobstructed.

steps.title: 6. Verify Chemistry Supply
steps.instructions: Confirm that the approved detergent or chemistry is available, correctly connected, and not obviously depleted or leaking. Do not compensate for poor cleaning by changing validated dosing settings without authorization. Expected outcome: Required chemistry is available to the washer.

steps.title: 7. Verify Water, Steam, and Drainage Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm required facility utilities are available and that the washer drains normally without standing water. Poor utility conditions or incomplete drainage can contribute to poor results or wet loads. Expected outcome: External utility and drainage conditions are normal.

steps.title: 8. Confirm Correct Cycle Selection
steps.instructions: Verify that the selected cycle is appropriate for the type of load being processed. Do not alter validated cycle parameters in an attempt to improve performance. Expected outcome: The normal approved cycle for the load is being used.

steps.title: 9. Run a Controlled Test Load
steps.instructions: After correcting any obvious external cause, run an approved representative or test load and inspect the outcome according to facility procedure.
