Expected outcome: The load exits acceptably clean and with expected drainage or drying performance. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Poor Performance
steps.instructions: If loading, spray access, chemistry, utilities, drainage, and cycle selection are correct but performance remains poor, remove the washer from service. Expected outcome: Potential circulation, heating, drying, chemistry-delivery, or control problems are escalated to qualified service.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported carts were exiting the Reliance Vision with visible soil remaining on lower surfaces.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found debris partially obstructing accessible spray nozzles in the chamber.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleared the accessible obstruction, ran a representative test load, and verified acceptable cleaning performance before returning the washer to service.

title: STERIS Reliance Vision Cart Washer - Printer, Cycle Record, or Tracking Interface Fails
description: Addresses missing printouts, incomplete cycle records, or tracking communication problems caused by paper, cabling, connectivity, configuration, or infrastructure issues.

steps.title: 1. Protect Process Documentation
steps.instructions: Determine whether the failure affects only convenience printing or whether required cycle traceability and release documentation are unavailable. Follow facility downtime procedures if processing records cannot be captured reliably. Expected outcome: Required traceability is maintained while the documentation problem is investigated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the printer is blank, jammed, offline, producing incomplete output, or whether cycle records are missing from an external tracking system. Identify whether the washer itself completed the cycle normally. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to printing, local record generation, or external interface communication.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Printer Supplies and Accessible Conditions
steps.instructions: If an integrated or associated printer is used, confirm paper or other required media is present and loaded correctly. Check for an accessible jam, open cover, or obvious physical damage. Expected outcome: The printer has the required supply and no simple obstruction. If correcting the media condition restores printing, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Accessible Cables and Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect external data, printer, network, or interface cables for disconnection, loose seating, damage, or strain. Reseat only connections that are intended to be externally serviced and are safe to disconnect. Expected outcome: External communication paths are securely connected.

steps.title: 5. Check Network or Interface Status
steps.instructions: For tracking-system failures, confirm the washer's normal network connection and nearby infrastructure are available. Determine whether other equipment using the same tracking system is also affected. Expected outcome: A local device issue is distinguished from a broader network, server, or application outage.

steps.title: 6. Verify Normal Configuration Without Changing It
steps.instructions: Review normal operator-accessible communication or printer status information if available. Do not alter network addresses, interface mappings, tracking identifiers, or protected configuration values without an approved change process. Expected outcome: No obvious operator-level configuration issue is present.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Record Test
steps.instructions: Run or use an approved test process that generates a cycle record and confirm whether it appears at the local printer and any expected external system. Do not create undocumented clinical test loads solely for interface troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The record is generated and delivered through the expected path. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Coordinate With IT or the Tracking-System Owner
steps.instructions: If the washer appears to create records locally but they do not reach the external system, coordinate with IT or the system owner to check network, server, interface engine, or application availability. Expected outcome: Infrastructure problems are assigned to the appropriate support group rather than misdiagnosed as washer hardware failures.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Device-Side Failure
steps.instructions: If external cabling and infrastructure are normal but the washer cannot generate or transmit the expected record, remove the affected function from service as required by facility policy and escalate. Expected outcome: Internal printer, interface, software, or control issues are referred to qualified service.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported the Reliance Vision completed cycles normally but no cycle records were appearing in the tracking system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external network cable at the washer connection was loose.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering restored the connection and verified a test cycle record transferred successfully to the tracking system.

title: STERIS Reliance Vision Cart Washer - Overtemperature, Leak, or Water-on-Floor Condition Occurs
description: Addresses overheating indications, visible leakage, or water around the washer caused by utilities, drainage, seals, hoses, loading, or service-level failures.

steps.title: 1. Protect Staff Immediately
steps.instructions: Stop use of the washer if there is uncontrolled hot water, steam, significant leakage, water near electrical equipment, burning odor, or an overtemperature indication. Keep personnel away from the affected area and follow facility spill and utility-isolation procedures. Expected outcome: Staff are protected from burns, slips, chemical exposure, and electrical hazards.

steps.title: 2. Remove the Washer from Service
steps.instructions: Do not start another cycle until the source of the condition has been identified and corrected. If safe and within facility procedure, place the equipment in its normal shutdown state. Involve Facilities for building utility isolation when required. Expected outcome: The hazardous condition is prevented from worsening.

steps.title: 3. Identify the Source Without Entering the Hazard Area
steps.instructions: Determine whether the water appears to originate from the door, supply piping, drain connection, chemistry tubing, chamber overflow, or an external facility source. Do not remove panels or reach into areas containing hot water, steam, energized components, or chemicals. Expected outcome: The likely external source category is identified safely.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Door and Seal Areas
steps.instructions: After the machine is safe and cool, inspect accessible door sealing surfaces for debris, damage, or a load interfering with closure. Check whether water trails originate specifically from the door perimeter. Expected outcome: A simple sealing obstruction is either identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Hoses and Connections
steps.instructions: Check visible water, drain, and chemistry connections for looseness, cracks, kinks, or active leakage. Do not tighten or repair pressurized facility plumbing unless it falls within authorized responsibilities. Expected outcome: Accessible external connections are intact, or a correctable external leak source is identified.

steps.title: 6. Check Facility Drainage
steps.instructions: Inspect surrounding drains for backup or slow flow. A washer discharge may appear to be a machine leak when a floor or connected drain cannot accept the flow. Escalate infrastructure drainage problems to Facilities. Expected outcome: Facility drainage is confirmed normal or identified as the source.

steps.title: 7. Confirm the Overtemperature Condition
steps.instructions: If the complaint involves overheating rather than a visible leak, record the displayed indication and cycle phase. Do not repeatedly restart the unit to see whether the condition recurs. Expected outcome: The abnormal temperature condition is documented without exposing the washer to repeated stress.

steps.title: 8. Correct Only Safe External Causes
steps.instructions: Remove accessible debris from a sealing surface, correct an improperly positioned load, or address an approved external connection only when safe and within Clinical Engineering scope. Do not bypass temperature protection or safety controls. Expected outcome: Any identified external cause is corrected without compromising safety systems.

steps.title: 9. Perform Controlled Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After the area is dry and safe and the cause has been corrected, run an approved test cycle while observing the washer from outside the hazard zone. Check for recurrence of leakage, abnormal heat, alarms, drainage problems, or water accumulation. Expected outcome: The washer completes the test cycle without leakage, overtemperature indication, or water accumulation. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Any Unexplained or Recurrent Hazard
steps.instructions: If the source cannot be confidently identified, if leakage recurs, or if an overtemperature condition returns, stop troubleshooting and keep the washer out of service. Expected outcome: A potentially serious internal or infrastructure problem is escalated rather than repeatedly tested.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported water accumulating on the floor in front of the Reliance Vision during wash cycles.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found debris on the loading-door sealing surface preventing complete closure.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the debris, cleaned the accessible sealing surface, and verified a full test cycle completed without leakage.
